sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Which three items must you carry whenever you drive, and what vehicle condition should you verify first?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Before driving, make sure you carry your valid driver license, proof of insurance and the vehicle registration, and check that the car is in good working order.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Before putting the car in motion, what belt and visibility steps must you finish inside the cabin?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Before moving, buckle your own seat belt, see that every passenger is buckled, and adjust the seat and mirrors so you can see out of every window.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: What does right-of-way determine where paths meet, and what assumption about vehicles on the right is dangerous?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Right-of-way decides who proceeds first and who waits, especially where drivers or pedestrians meet without signals or signs, and you should never assume the vehicle on the right automatically goes first.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Regardless of technical priority rules, when does Wisconsin law always require you to yield?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Whatever the situation, you are always required to yield when that is needed to avoid striking a pedestrian, a bicyclist or another vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Which road users already inside an intersection keep priority over waiting traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers who are still in the intersection.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Who proceeds first at a four-way stop, and how is a simultaneous arrival broken?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: At a four-way stop the first driver or bicyclist to arrive goes first, and when two or more arrive together the driver on the right goes first.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: At a four-way stop, does sitting to another driver's right let you go ahead if they stopped earlier?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: At a four-way stop, arrival order decides who goes, and the driver on the right wins only as the tie-breaker when drivers arrive at the same moment.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: When you reach an open intersection with zero signs or signals, which direction gets priority?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or signals, yield to vehicles approaching from your right.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Whom must you yield to when entering a roundabout or reaching an uncontrolled T-intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Yield to traffic already circulating in a roundabout, and to cross traffic at an uncontrolled T-intersection.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Contrast who gets the right-of-way at an uncontrolled four-way corner versus an uncontrolled T-intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: Yielding to the vehicle on your right is the rule for an uncontrolled intersection, but at an uncontrolled T-intersection you yield to the cross traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: As you approach a roundabout entrance, which stream of vehicles holds the right-of-way?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Entering a roundabout, the vehicles you yield to are the ones already circulating inside it.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: How far back must you stop for a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, and how long do you wait?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Yield to a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or carries a white cane even if that person is not in the intersection, stopping at least ten feet away until the person has left the roadway.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: Does a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog lose priority when crossing away from an intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: A blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane keeps the right-of-way even outside the intersection, and you must stop at least ten feet away until the person clears the road.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which vehicles keep priority when someone passes you, when you turn left or U-turn, or when sirens sound?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Yield to a vehicle passing you on either side in your direction, to oncoming vehicles when you turn left or make a U-turn, and to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Before turning left or swinging a U-turn, or while being overtaken on either side, whom do you let go?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Turning left or making a U-turn, you yield to oncoming vehicles, and you also yield to any vehicle overtaking you on the left or the right.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: What core safety goal should govern your speed choice, and what named Wisconsin rule gauges your following gap?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: Choose a speed that always leaves you able to stop safely, and measure your gap with the Four Second Following Distance Rule.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: How do you use a roadside landmark to measure a four-second following gap, and what proves you are too close?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: To apply the four-second rule, pick a fixed object ahead such as a tree, sign or house and count from one thousand one to one thousand four; reaching the object before you finish means you are going too fast.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: How do you adjust your four-second following count when rain, snow, ice, or heavy traffic show up?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Add one extra second to the following count for each adverse condition, such as heavier traffic, rain, snow or ice.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: What is Wisconsin's baseline following time gap, and how much time does each poor condition tack onto it?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: The four-second count is a following gap, and each adverse condition such as rain, snow, ice or heavier traffic adds one more second.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What does a posted speed limit represent legally, and may you push above it to pass a slower car?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: A speed limit is the highest legal speed for the area, exceeding the posted limit is illegal, and you may not speed up past the limit to pass another vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Is a driver ever allowed to exceed the posted speed limit briefly to finish passing another vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Passing does not permit speeding: you may not exceed the posted limit even briefly to get around another vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: How does Wisconsin law treat racing and reckless driving, and what roadside check keeps your speed legal?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Racing and reckless driving are illegal, so keep scanning the roadside for the posted speed limit sign.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: When no speed sign is posted in a Wisconsin residential neighborhood, what limit applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: Unless a sign says otherwise, the speed limit in residential areas is twenty-five miles per hour

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: What is the standard Wisconsin school-zone speed limit when children are present?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: The usual school zone limit when children are present is fifteen miles per hour

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: In unposted outlying sections of Wisconsin cities and villages, what maximum speed limit applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: In the outlying parts of cities and villages where no limit is posted, the maximum is thirty-five miles per hour

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Compare Wisconsin's default speed limits across active school zones, residential blocks, and unposted outlying town edges?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: The residential default is twenty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise, the school zone limit with children present is fifteen miles per hour, and unposted outlying areas of cities and villages top out at thirty-five miles per hour

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Why might driving right at the posted speed limit still be unsafe on a foggy or slick day?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: The limit is a maximum, so poor visibility or road conditions may call for a slower speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Why can creeping far below traffic speed trigger crashes and earn a police ticket just like speeding?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Driving either too fast or too slow can cause a crash, because slow drivers make traffic stack up behind them, and police can ticket you for either.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Which lane belongs to you when traveling slower than surrounding traffic on a multi-lane road?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: If you drive slower than most traffic on a multi-lane road, use the far-right lane.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: How do you avoid impeding-traffic tickets and crashes when others move faster on a multi-lane road?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: Driving too slowly can also earn a ticket and cause crashes, so the safe choice is to match traffic and use the far-right lane when slower.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: What speed should you target in flowing traffic and while merging onto a highway?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Try to match the speed of surrounding traffic, and when merging, enter at the speed the traffic is moving without forcing anyone to brake or swerve.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: How should you use a highway on-ramp's acceleration lane, and whose duty is finding a safe merging gap?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: On a highway you use the acceleration lane of the on-ramp to build speed as you merge, and finding a safe, legal gap is your responsibility.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: Even if through drivers sometimes courtesy-shift left, who bears legal responsibility for merging safely from an on-ramp?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: When merging from an on-ramp, the merging driver is the one responsible for finding a safe gap, even though highway traffic may slow or move over.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: Where should your gradual braking happen when exiting a highway?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: When leaving a highway, move into the deceleration lane of the off-ramp and slow down gradually there, checking around you as you leave traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Pair the highway acceleration lane and deceleration lane with their ramps and speed changes?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: The acceleration lane is on the on-ramp and is used to speed up, while the deceleration lane is on the off-ramp and is used to slow down.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What happens to the space needed for turning, slowing, or stopping as your speed climbs?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: The faster you travel, the more distance you need to turn, slow down or stop, so adjust speed to road and traffic conditions.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: How many seconds down the road ahead should you scan to maintain solid vehicle control?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: For good control you need to see ten to fifteen seconds ahead of your vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: Does Wisconsin's ten-to-fifteen-second rule measure following distance or visual look-ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: Seeing ten to fifteen seconds ahead is about how far down the road you look, not about how far behind the next vehicle you follow.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: Which road shapes, busy places, and fresh weather call for slowing down, and what is best on icy roads?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.memory_hook: Slow for curves, crowds; skip ice
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Slow down on curves and hills, when rain, snow or hail begins, in parking lots, malls and downtown areas, near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, and in heavy traffic; avoid driving at all on icy roads if you can.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Beyond standard street corners, which everyday crossings count as intersections under Wisconsin rules?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: An intersection is any place where two paths cross, which includes cross streets, driveways, parking lot entrances and railroad crossings.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: What three things must you verify before rolling into any intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Before entering an intersection, look left and right, make sure no vehicles or pedestrians are in it, and check for a clear path to where you are going.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: How should you handle an intersection when obstructions block your cross-street view?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: If you cannot see well into an intersection, edge forward carefully and stay ready to brake, especially where there are no signals or signs.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: Which three common roadside objects hide approaching cross traffic near intersections, and how should you approach?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Trees, buildings and parked vehicles can hide cross traffic, so approach a blocked intersection slowly.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: Even with a green light, why must your intersection check sweep left, then right, then left once more?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.memory_hook: Left, right, left; others blow signs
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: Because some drivers miss or ignore signs and signals, search left, right and left again before crossing, even when you have the right-of-way.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: What two crash risks come from slamming the brakes late instead of spotting slowdowns early?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: Watching far ahead lets you begin slowing early, because a sudden stop can make you lose control or get you rear-ended, while early braking gives a gradual, safer stop.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: Why must you keep your transmission in gear rather than coasting in neutral while moving?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: Do not coast in neutral; keep the car in gear so you have full control.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.front: What driving habit is called coasting, and why does Wisconsin's handbook tell you to avoid it?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.expected_back: Coasting means rolling in neutral, and the handbook says to stay in gear instead so you keep full control of the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: When curves, hills, darkness, or fog cut your forward view under ten to fifteen seconds, what is required?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: The sight distance rule says that when your view ahead is shorter than ten to fifteen seconds of travel, you are required to reduce speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: Which four directions around your vehicle should regular driving and mirror checks cover?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: Check all your mirrors while driving, looking left, right, ahead and behind with the rearview mirror.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: What four checks protect you before driving across railroad tracks?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: At a railroad crossing never assume no train is coming: stop before the crossing, look both ways, listen, and make sure there is room for your car on the far side.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.front: Besides looking and listening for an approaching train, what space check is mandatory before entering railroad tracks?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.expected_back: At a railroad crossing the check is twofold: look and listen for a train, and confirm space for your whole car beyond the tracks before crossing.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.front: Why should you keep eyes moving forward instead of staring at traffic stops or roadside scenes?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.expected_back: Do not stare at drivers who have been pulled over or at other roadside activity, because that distraction can cause a crash.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.front: How should you manage space around large trucks and cars lingering right beside your doors?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.expected_back: Keep space on every side of your car, give large vehicles extra room so you can see around them and they can see you, and move ahead of or behind a vehicle riding right beside you when safe.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.front: Which standard time-gap rule sets your forward buffer whenever following another vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.expected_back: For space in front, apply the four-second following distance rule whenever you are behind another vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F41.front: Which road surfaces, passing situations, and lead vehicles require stretching your gap past four seconds?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.expected_back: Leave more than four seconds ahead on slippery, icy or snowy roads, when the driver behind wants to pass, and when following trucks, buses, vans, large vehicles, motorcycles or bicycles.

sec03-card-sec03-F42.front: Which five load, rear-traffic, emergency, rail, or grade situations call for more than four seconds ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.expected_back: Also leave extra following time when hauling a heavy load or trailer, when someone is tailgating you, when emergency vehicles are ahead, at railroad crossings, and when stopping on a hill.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.front: Along with following motorcycles or bicycles, which two stopping or crossing spots require extra room ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.expected_back: Stopping on a hill and approaching a railroad crossing are both reasons to leave extra seconds in front, along with following motorcycles or bicycles.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.front: How often should you glance at your rearview mirror, and what is the safe response to a tailgater?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.expected_back: Check the rearview mirror every six to eight seconds for tailgaters, and if someone is following too closely, slow down gradually to encourage them to pass.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.front: Contrast Wisconsin's six-to-eight-second rhythm against its four-second rule so you never mix them up?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.expected_back: Checking the rearview mirror every six to eight seconds is a different number from the four-second following gap, and it is meant to spot tailgaters.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.front: According to Wisconsin's handbook, how do you safely encourage a close tailgater to go around you?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.expected_back: The handbook response to a tailgater is a gradual slowdown, which encourages that driver to go around you.

sec03-card-sec03-F44.front: Which two habits help drivers behind you anticipate your moves, and whose blind rear needs extra room?
sec03-card-sec03-F44.expected_back: Help drivers behind you by holding a steady speed and signaling well before you slow or turn, and give extra room to a driver who cannot see behind their own vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F45.front: Where must passenger pick-ups happen, and how should a slower driver handle multi-lane traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F45.expected_back: To pick up or drop off passengers, find a safe spot out of traffic; if you are slower than most traffic on a multi-lane road, keep right and pull over so others can pass on the left.

sec03-card-sec03-F46.front: Before driving across opposing traffic or a multi-lane roadway, what three checks keep you from getting stranded?
sec03-card-sec03-F46.expected_back: Before crossing traffic or a multi-lane road, make sure there is room to clear it completely, check for vehicles and pedestrians, and wait until it is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What five checks and actions must you complete before starting any turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Before any turn, check your mirrors, your surroundings and your blind spot, stay in your lane, signal your turn and yield the right-of-way.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Why are last-second changes of plan unsafe, and what must you check before turning into a driveway?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Last-second changes of plan are unsafe and can cause a crash, so check mirrors and the traffic behind you before turning into a side road or driveway.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: What two lane errors must you avoid mid-turn, and why do trucks and buses need extra space?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Do not change lanes in the middle of a turn or cut across the center line, and leave extra room for trucks and buses, which may swing over the center line as they turn.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: If a turning bus swings across the center stripe, may your car cross it too, or what should you do?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Large trucks and buses may swing across the center line while turning, but you must not cross it yourself, so give them extra room instead.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: How should you position your car, scan for walkers, and wait inside an intersection for a left turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: For a left turn, check that your path is clear, keep near the center line, watch for pedestrians crossing on the left, and wait about halfway into the intersection while leaving room for oncoming turners.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Which way must your front wheels point while waiting to turn left, and what happens if rear-ended otherwise?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: While waiting to turn left, keep the steering wheel and wheels straight, because if you are hit from behind with the wheel turned left you will be pushed into oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: How does a U-turn reverse your travel direction, and how risky is it even where legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: A U-turn is one smooth U-shaped motion that reverses your direction, and it can be very dangerous even though some intersections allow it.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What three things must you verify before starting any U-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Before a U-turn, check all mirrors and traffic and look for any sign that prohibits it.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Under what condition is a U-turn legal on any rural two-lane highway?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: On any rural two-lane highway a U-turn is allowed as long as it is done safely and does not interfere with traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: What motion defines a proper U-turn, and what can override its rural two-lane permission?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: A U-turn is a single continuous motion and is allowed on any rural two-lane highway when safe, unless a sign forbids it.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: When two or more lanes turn together at an intersection, which lane must you finish in?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: With multiple turn lanes, finish the turn in the matching lane: start in the left-most lane and end in the left-most lane, start in the middle and end in the middle.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Which lane must you occupy before making a right turn off a four-lane road?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: When turning right from a four-lane roadway, the turn must be made from the lane closest to the right curb or road edge.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: On what kind of street belongs a Y-turn, and what official test requires you to demonstrate one?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Use a Y-turn only in residential areas on streets too narrow for a U-turn; you will also be asked to perform one on the driving exam.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does a Y-turn differ in motion, setting, and exam testing from a U-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: A Y-turn is a stop-and-reverse turnaround reserved for residential streets too narrow for a U-turn, and it is also a graded maneuver on the driving exam.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: What exact sequence of signaling, checking, positioning, and stopping makes up step one of a Y-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Y-turn step one: signal right, check your mirrors and the traffic on your right, move over as far to the right as possible, and stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: What four actions take you across the street in step two of a Y-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Y-turn step two is to signal left, check your blind spot, turn left across to the opposite curb and stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: How do you execute step three's reverse and step four's pull-away to finish a Y-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Y-turn step three is to look back over your right shoulder and reverse just far enough to drive forward again, then stop; step four is to check left and right and pull forward into your lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: Which numbered step of the Y-turn is the sole reversing move, and where must you look first?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: In the Y-turn the only reversing step is the third one, where you look back over your right shoulder before backing.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Under what two narrow conditions may you drive onto a paved shoulder to pass another vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: You may use a paved shoulder to get around a vehicle only when that vehicle is stopped or is making a left turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Which lane handles passing on multi-lane highways, and why is overtaking on the right dangerous?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: On a multi-lane road the left-most lane is the lane for going around slower vehicles, and passing on the right is risky because the other driver may not see you.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How does standard highway overtaking contrast with passing along a paved shoulder?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Passing on the left is the normal pass, while going around on a paved shoulder is allowed only past a stopped or left-turning vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: What two courteous, safety-first actions should you take whenever another vehicle tries to pass you?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: If another driver is trying to pass you, keep to your lane and slow down.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: What four-part routine must you follow every single time you change lanes?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Before changing lanes, make sure the way is clear, signal first, move only one lane at a time, and look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What do we call the zones checked over your left and right shoulders, and why can mirrors not cover them?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: The areas you check over your left and right shoulders are blind spots, which cannot be seen by using your mirrors alone.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Why does glancing at rearview and side mirrors alone fall short right before switching lanes?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Checking mirrors is not enough before a lane change, because the blind spots are seen only by looking over the shoulder toward the new lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: How many vehicles may you overtake in one pass, on which side, and why?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Pass only one vehicle at a time and only on the left, since there may not be time to get around several vehicles or even the one ahead of you.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: May you hang out in the passing lane or push above the posted speed limit to finish overtaking?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Do not linger in the passing lane, and never exceed the speed limit to complete a pass.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: What space must exist ahead of the car you pass before pulling out, and must other drivers make room?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Pass only when there is enough room in front of the vehicle you are passing, and remember that other drivers are not required to move over for you.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How does Wisconsin law treat the speed limit and the passed driver's lane duty while you overtake?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: The speed limit still applies while passing, and the vehicle being passed has no duty to move over for you.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What exact sight in your inside rearview mirror confirms you have cleared a passed vehicle enough to merge right?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: It is safe to return to the driving lane once both headlights of the vehicle you passed appear in your rearview mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: After overtaking on the left, how do you verify clean buffer space before pulling back into the travel lane?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: After passing, the cue that it is safe to move back into the driving lane is seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Because rear visibility is tight, how far and how fast should you ever drive in reverse?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Because it is hard to see behind a vehicle, back up as little as possible and no faster than a slow walk.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: Instead of trusting mirrors and cameras alone while backing, how should you position your body and get help?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: When backing, do not rely only on your mirrors and backup camera: turn your body, look over your right shoulder through the rear window, and use a helper outside the car when you can.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: What scan comes right after backing, and how must you handle missing a highway exit or street turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: After backing, scan left and right before rejoining traffic, and if you miss an exit or turn, never back up; continue to the next exit and come back.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: If you sail right past your highway exit ramp, what is the sole safe recovery move?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: A missed exit is handled by driving to the next exit and coming back, never by backing up on the road.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: Whose responsibility is keeping a parked car hazard-free, and where does that normally place your car?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: You are responsible for making sure your parked vehicle is not a hazard, which normally means parking on the far-right side, clear of any travel lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: Which three curb markings, fixtures, or posts forbid parking your vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: Parking is not allowed along yellow-marked curbs, in front of fire hydrants, or where a No Parking sign is posted.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: At what speed should you pull into a spot, and how do you secure automatic or manual cars on flat ground?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: Park at a very low speed, and on level ground shift into Park, or into gear with a manual transmission, and set the parking brake.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: Which direction must you turn your front wheels before shifting into park when facing uphill beside a curb?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Parked uphill with a curb, turn the wheels all the way to the left before shifting into park.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking uphill along a road with no curb?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Parked uphill without a curb, turn the wheels all the way to the right before shifting into park.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: Which way do your front wheels turn when parked downhill, and what brake rule applies on every slope?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: Parked downhill, turn the wheels all the way to the right, and on any hill set the emergency brake.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Out of all hill-parking setups, which sole setup turns wheels left while every other case turns right?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Uphill with a curb is the left-wheel case, while uphill without a curb and every downhill park are right-wheel cases.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: What hazards must you scan for before parallel parking, and how much longer than your car should the gap measure?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: For parallel parking between vehicles, watch for traffic, pedestrians and fixed objects, and look for a space about three-six feet longer than your vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: How do you signal and position your car alongside the front parked vehicle to start parallel parking?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Parallel parking starts with your turn signal on and a stop alongside the vehicle ahead of the space, about two feet away from it.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: In parallel parking, how does your side-by-side starting gap compare with the extra length needed in the curb space?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: When you begin parallel parking you stop about two feet from the car ahead, and the space you choose should be about three-six feet longer than your car.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: Once stopped parallel to the lead car, which way do you crank the wheel and how do you start moving?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: Next, turn the wheel fully toward the side you are parking on, left for the left side of the road and right for the right side, and back up slowly.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: What alignment landmark tells you to straighten the steering wheel and glide straight back into the space?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: When your front door passes the rear bumper of the car you are parking behind, straighten the wheel and keep backing slowly in a straight line.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: What clearance landmark cues you to crank the steering wheel sharply the opposite way while backing in?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: Once your bumper clears the vehicle in front, turn the wheel sharply the other way and back slowly until you are parallel to the curb.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: How do you finish positioning your wheels, curb gap, and front-and-rear bumper cushions in a parallel spot?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: Finish by straightening the wheels, ending about a foot from the curb and at least two feet from the vehicles ahead and behind.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: At the end of a clean parallel park, how does your target distance from the curb differ from your distance to other cars?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: At the end of a parallel park you should be about a foot from the curb, but at least two feet from the vehicles ahead and behind.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: What four lighting or braking tools plus space habit broadcast your position and plans to surrounding drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Let other drivers know where you are and what you intend by using headlights, brakes, turn signals and hazard lights, and by keeping space ahead and behind.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.front: Why should you stay out of the driver's seat when feeling intensely worried, excited, afraid, angry, or down?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.expected_back: Strong emotions affect safe driving, so do not drive when you are very worried, excited, afraid, angry or depressed.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.front: What safety purpose does the horn serve, and when do you use a light tap versus a hard press?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.expected_back: The horn exists to help prevent crashes: a light tap gets another driver's attention, and a hard press warns of a collision about to happen.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: How do you match horn pressure to polite awareness versus an imminent crash?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: A light tap on the horn is for getting attention, while a hard press is reserved for warning of an imminent collision.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.front: Even if your car features automatic daytime sensors, what manual headlight habit must you still know?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.expected_back: Low beams help you see and be seen; even if your car switches them on automatically, learn the manual control and check that they come on when needed.

sec04-card-sec04-F43.front: What sight distance limit and exact sunset-to-sunrise window make low-beam headlights legally mandatory?
sec04-card-sec04-F43.expected_back: Low beams are required when you cannot see a vehicle or person five hundred feet away, about one block, and from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise.

sec04-card-sec04-F44.front: Under what wiper and weather conditions does the manual recommend switching on your low beams?
sec04-card-sec04-F44.expected_back: Low beams are recommended whenever your windshield wipers are on and in rain, snow or fog.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.front: How does Wisconsin separate legally required low-beam situations from recommended low-beam situations?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.expected_back: Low beams are required at the five hundred-foot visibility threshold and in the half hour after sunset through the half hour before sunrise, but are only recommended with wipers on or in rain, snow or fog.

sec04-card-sec04-F45.front: How much farther do high beams reach than low beams, where do they help, and when must you dim them?
sec04-card-sec04-F45.expected_back: High beams let you see twice as far as low beams; use them when no vehicles are approaching or in an unfamiliar place or construction area, and dim them for oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F46.front: Where should your eyes look against blinding oncoming brights, and when is the sole time to use parking lights?
sec04-card-sec04-F46.expected_back: If an oncoming driver leaves the high beams on, look toward the right side of the road, and use parking lights only while parked and idling.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.front: How do high beams and parking lights stand at opposite ends of driving versus stationary use?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.expected_back: High beams double your seeing distance compared with low beams, yet must be dimmed when a vehicle approaches; parking lights are only for when you are parked and idling.

sec04-card-sec04-F47.front: What sequence comes before moving, and how early in time and distance do you signal an intersection turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F47.expected_back: Turn on your signal, check around you, and then move; at an intersection, begin signaling about three seconds, roughly one hundred feet, before the turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F48.front: When your target driveway sits right beyond an intersection, at what moment should you flick on your blinker?
sec04-card-sec04-F48.expected_back: When your turn comes just after an intersection, wait until you have crossed the intersection before signaling.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.front: How does blinker timing shift between turning at the cross street versus turning into a lot just beyond it?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.expected_back: At an intersection you signal about three seconds, roughly one hundred feet, ahead of the turn, but for a turn just past an intersection you wait until you have crossed it.

sec04-card-sec04-F49.front: When may hand gestures stand in for blinkers, and what left-arm position marks left, right, and slow or stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F49.expected_back: Hand signals may replace turn signals that are missing or hard to see: arm straight out the driver window to turn left, elbow bent with the hand up to turn right, and hand pointed down to slow or stop.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.front: How do the three driver-side arm angles map to left turn, right turn, and braking?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.expected_back: In hand signals a straight arm means a left turn, an arm bent upward means a right turn, and an arm pointed down means slowing or stopping.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Where do traffic signals typically stand, and how are red, yellow, and green stacked from top to bottom?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Traffic signals usually stand at intersections and stack red on top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Instead of a full three-lens housing, what simpler setup hangs over many rural country intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Many intersections out in the country have only a single yellow or red light.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: How must you treat an intersection whenever its traffic signal loses power or malfunctions?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: If a traffic light has no power or is not working properly, treat the intersection as if it had a stop sign.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: When a traffic light goes dark or glitches out, which control rule applies instead of a yield or green?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A traffic light that is out or malfunctioning is handled like a stop sign, not like a yield sign or a green light.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Whose command wins when a uniformed police officer directs traffic underneath a working signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: When a police officer is directing traffic at a signal, follow the officer's directions.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What two conditions must happen after your complete stop at a steady red light before going straight?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: At a steady red light, stop completely and wait until the light turns green and cross traffic has cleared.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: What two-step sequence applies when you roll up to a flashing red traffic light?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: At a flashing red light, stop completely and then go when it is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: After halting your wheels completely, how does a steady red light differ from a flashing red light?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Both a steady red and a flashing red require a full stop, but after a flashing red you may go once it is safe, while after a steady red you wait for green.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: What must you do when facing a steady red turn arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: At a steady red arrow, stop completely and wait for the light to turn green.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: How do you handle a turn lane controlled by a flashing red arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: At a flashing red arrow, stop completely and then go when it is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: What separates your post-stop move at a steady red arrow from your move at a flashing red arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: A steady red arrow means stop and wait for green, while a flashing red arrow means stop and then go when safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: What two conditions make turning right on a steady red light legal in Wisconsin?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: You may turn right on a steady red when it is safe and no sign forbids the turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What exact street-to-street combination is required to make a legal left turn on red?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: A left turn on red is allowed only when you are turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How do street-type restrictions differ between turning right on red and turning left on red?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Right turns on red are allowed whenever safe and not forbidden by a sign, but left turns on red only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: How must every legal turn on red start, handle conflicting road users, and finish?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Any turn on red starts with a full stop; then yield to all traffic and complete the turn staying in your lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: What phase comes right after steady yellow, and what must you do if you have not entered yet?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: A steady yellow light means red is coming, so slow down and stop before you enter the intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: What should you do if the signal switches to yellow after your car is already inside the intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, do not stop; keep going through.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: What three-step habit applies when approaching a flashing yellow signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: At a flashing yellow light, slow down, look for cross traffic and go ahead with caution.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Before you reach the crosswalk, how does steady yellow differ from flashing yellow?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: A steady yellow means stop before the intersection if you have not entered it, while a flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: What transition does a steady yellow arrow announce, and how should you respond?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow means the arrow is about to turn red, and you should stop if you can do so safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: How do you safely complete a turn under a flashing yellow arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: At a flashing yellow arrow, yield before making the turn and then proceed with caution.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How does the meaning of a steady yellow arrow contrast with a flashing yellow arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow warns the arrow is about to turn red, while a flashing yellow arrow lets you turn after yielding.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: Even when cruising straight on a steady green light, whom must you still yield to?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: A steady green light lets you go through the intersection, but you must still yield to emergency vehicles and others the law requires.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: When you sit first in line and your red light flips green, what must happen before you pull out?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: If you were stopped and the light turns green, let cross traffic clear the intersection before you go.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Why may you turn left on a steady circular green light only when a clean gap opens?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: On a steady green you may turn left only when it is safe, because oncoming traffic has the right-of-way.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: What traffic protection comes with a steady green arrow, and whom must you still watch out for?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: A steady green arrow lets you turn the way it points with no oncoming or crossing traffic expected, but you still watch for pedestrians.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: How does turning left on a steady green ball contrast with turning left under a steady green arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: On a steady green ball a left turn must yield to oncoming traffic, while under a green arrow no oncoming or crossing traffic should be moving.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Why does neither a green arrow nor a steady green ball ever grant blind, unconditional right-of-way?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Even on a green arrow you still watch for pedestrians, and even on a steady green you still yield to emergency vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: What four things do pavement lines, symbols, and stripe colors tell you about the road beneath your tires?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Lines and symbols on the pavement divide the road into lanes, show where passing and lane changes are allowed and which lanes are for turns, and their color tells you whether the road is one-way or two-way.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Which color stripe marks your right travel edge, and which color marks the left edge of lanes going your way?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: A solid white line marks the right edge of the travel lane, and a solid or dashed yellow line marks the left edge of the lanes going your way.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: How do white interior stripes and the left-side yellow stripe divide duties along your travel lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: White lines separate lanes going the same way, while the yellow line marks the left edge of the lanes going your way.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: What does a dashed white stripe allow, and what rule does a white pavement arrow set for its lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: White dashed lines separate lanes going the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe, and a white pavement arrow shows the direction that lane must go.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: Under Wisconsin rules, what are the sole two reasons you may cross a solid white line between lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: A solid white line between lanes may not be crossed except to avoid a hazard or when you are turning within the next block.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: How does Wisconsin's rule for crossing dashed white paint differ from crossing solid white paint between lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: A white dashed line may be crossed when safe, while a solid white line between lanes may be crossed only for a hazard or a turn within the next block.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Where exact spot must your front tires stop near a crosswalk, and where must you never rest?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: At a crosswalk, stop with your front wheels just short of the solid white line and never stop on the crosswalk itself.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Besides street corners, where else can crosswalks sit, and what extra control might walkers have there?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Crosswalks are usually at intersections but sometimes sit in the middle of a block, and pedestrians there may have their own signals.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: What traffic directions do solid yellow stripes divide, and what general passing rule do two solid yellows set?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and two solid yellow lines mean neither direction may pass.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: When may you turn across a double solid yellow center line?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: You may cross a double solid yellow line to turn into a driveway when it is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: What slow-vehicle exception allows passing across double yellow in Wisconsin, and which vehicle is excluded?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: You may also cross it to pass a vehicle moving at less than half the speed limit when safe, but not if that vehicle is farm equipment.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: What are Wisconsin's two legal reasons to cross double solid yellow, plus the farm-machinery rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: The double yellow exceptions are turning into a driveway and passing a vehicle going under half the speed limit, and the second never applies to farm equipment.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: What maneuver does a single dashed yellow center line allow, and what caution stays in force?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: A dashed yellow line means you may pass when it is safe, while watching for other traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: How does standard passing permission contrast between a single dashed yellow line and double solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: A single dashed yellow line allows passing when safe, while two solid yellow lines forbid passing from either side.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: Where one dashed yellow stripe runs alongside one solid yellow stripe, who holds permission to pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: Where a dashed yellow line runs beside a solid one, only drivers on the dashed side may pass.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: Along mixed solid-and-dashed yellow center stripes, how do you know instantly whether passing applies to you?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: With a dashed line beside a solid yellow line, the line nearest you decides: dashed on your side allows passing, solid on your side does not.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: Besides yellow center paint, what else may mark where passing zones start and end?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: Some passing zones also have signs showing where passing is and is not allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: Which two maneuvers belong in a shared center lane, who may enter it, and what arrows mark it?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: A shared center lane is only for left turns and U-turns, can be used by traffic from either direction, and is marked with white left-turn arrows.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: When and why may you cross the outer solid yellow border into a shared center lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: You may cross the solid yellow line into a shared center lane to make a left turn or U-turn, but only enter it when it is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: How do reversible lanes schedule flow, and what pavement stripes and overhead hardware control them?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: Reversible lanes run on different hours for each lane, are marked with double dashed yellow lines, and use special overhead lights to show which lanes you may use.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.front: How do shared center turn lanes and reversible lanes differ in both yellow edge stripes and purpose?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.expected_back: A shared center lane is marked with solid and dashed yellow lines and is used only for left turns and U-turns, while a reversible lane is marked with double dashed yellow lines and has different operating hours for each lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: Above a reversible lane, what does a red X, a green arrow, and a yellow X each command?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.memory_hook: Red closed, green open, yellow vacate
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: Over a reversible lane, a red X means the lane is closed, a green arrow means it is open, and a yellow X means it is changing, so move into a lane with a green arrow.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: Who may travel in a reserved lane, what symbol often marks it, and may other cars cruise there?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: Reserved lanes are only for the type of vehicle named on the sign, are often marked with a white diamond on the sign and pavement, and are illegal to use in any other vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.front: How close to your corner may you enter a reserved lane to turn, and how do you handle cyclists there?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.expected_back: You may drive in a reserved lane to turn across it within the next half of a block, and if a bicyclist is in it, move in behind them and turn when safe.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.front: What exact distance cap limits how early general traffic can enter a reserved lane for a turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.expected_back: A reserved lane may be entered by other vehicles only to turn across it within the next half of a block.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.front: What time details are often posted on bus and carpool lane boards?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.expected_back: Signs for bus and car pool lanes may list the days and hours when the restriction applies.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.front: Which three surface paint colors may highlight bus and bike lanes, and what guides your move?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.expected_back: Bus and bike lanes may be painted in colors such as red, green or gray; follow the pavement lettering and posted signs.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.front: What is a highway flex lane, what stripe borders it, and what triggers its opening?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.expected_back: On some highways signs allow the paved shoulder to be used as a flex lane, which is separated by a solid yellow line and opened according to traffic volume and special events.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.front: Which class of vehicles is strictly prohibited from driving in a Wisconsin flex lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.expected_back: Large trucks may not drive in a flex lane.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.front: Even when a green overhead arrow opens a highway flex lane, may large trucks pull into it?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.expected_back: A flex lane is the paved shoulder opened by signs as a travel lane, but large trucks may never use it even when its green arrow is lit.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.front: If a crash or stalled car blocks a flex lane ahead, how do overhead beacons redirect traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.expected_back: If there is an incident along a flex lane, yellow and red X signals tell drivers to merge into the next lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.front: Above a Wisconsin flex lane, what do the green arrow, yellow X, and red X each mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.expected_back: Over a flex lane, a green arrow means open, a yellow X means it is closing so merge into the general-purpose lanes, and a red X means closed.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.front: Over a flex lane, how does a yellow X differ in urgency and meaning from a red X?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.expected_back: In a flex lane a yellow X means the lane is closing so you merge into the general-purpose lanes, while a red X means it is already closed.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.front: Which roadside panel marks the downstream end of a flex lane, and where do you move?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.expected_back: A Merge sign marks the end of the flex lane, where you merge back into the general-purpose lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What two prep steps belong before every trip, and what is the smartest call when roads look icy or unsafe?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Plan ahead and check your vehicle before you leave, and stay home when the roads look icy or unsafe.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: What does the handbook call heavily worn tires, and how do they hurt bad-weather safety?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.memory_hook: Bald tires cut grip, stretch stops
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Heavily worn tires are called bald tires, and they lower traction and lengthen stopping distance, which is especially dangerous in bad weather.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: Which two distinct mechanical drawbacks make bald tires dangerous?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Bald tires do two separate kinds of harm: they reduce traction and they make stopping distances longer.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: How does reduced visibility trick your eyes when judging the speed of other vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: When visibility is reduced, other vehicles can seem to move slower than they really are.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Why shouldn't you trust that a slow-looking car in fog or heavy rain is taking its time?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: In poor visibility, a vehicle that looks slow may actually be moving faster than it appears.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Which two things become harder to judge about oncoming traffic after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: At night it is harder to judge how far away oncoming vehicles are and how fast they are going.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What three adjustments should you make whenever fog, rain, or haze cuts visibility?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: In fog, rain or other low-visibility conditions, slow down, be ready to stop and use your headlights to see better.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What is the best decision when roads are snow-packed, icy, slippery, or flooded by downpours?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: When roads are slippery, icy, snow covered or flooded with heavy rain, the best choice is to stay off the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: During cold severe weather, which parts of a highway freeze over before regular roadbed?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: In severe weather, bridges and overpasses freeze before the rest of the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: On cold, damp days, which three spots along a route are prime hiding places for ice?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Watch for slippery or icy pavement in shady spots and on bridges and overpasses on cold, wet days.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: Why can your tires suddenly break loose on a bridge or shady bend when the open highway felt dry?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Ice forms first on bridges and overpasses and in shady spots, so these can be slippery even while the open road is not.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: Besides snow and bridges, which three everyday conditions make pavement surprisingly slippery?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.memory_hook: Near freezing, first rain, shoulder water
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Roads are also likely to be slippery when the temperature is near freezing, when rain first begins to fall, and where water stands near the shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Why are the opening minutes of a rain shower dangerous rather than mild?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: The first minutes of rain are a slippery time, not a safe one, because the handbook lists pavement just as it starts to rain among likely slick spots.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: When you have no choice and must drive on slick pavement, how should you handle speed, brakes, and steering?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: If you must drive on slick roads, slow down, stay alert and avoid hard braking or sudden sharp turns so you keep control.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: In a vehicle without anti-lock brakes, how do you slow down on slippery pavement without locking the wheels?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: In a car without an anti-lock braking system, gently pump the brakes to help keep it from skidding or sliding on slippery roads.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How does universal slick-road braking advice connect with the specific technique for cars without ABS?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Gently pumping the brakes is the advice for cars without ABS, while the general slick-road advice for every car is to avoid rapid braking.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: What happens during hydroplaning, and how do bald tires change the speed where it starts?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Hydroplaning means your tires are riding on top of water instead of the road, and with bald tires it can happen even at low speeds.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Which three exact moves bring your car safely through hydroplaning?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: If you begin to hydroplane, ease off the gas, keep the steering wheel straight, and do not brake or turn until the tires grip the road again.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Why must you resist both braking and steering while your tires are hydroplaning?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: When hydroplaning you neither brake nor turn until the tires grip the road again; you only ease off the gas and hold the wheel straight.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: How does the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook describe what your tires are doing during a skid?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: The handbook describes a skid as your tires bouncing on the road after you have lost control of the vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: When a skid starts, what do you do with your brake foot and your steering wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: In a skid, stay off the brake and steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What steering adjustment must you make right as a skidding car begins to straighten out?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: As soon as the car starts to straighten out of a skid, turn the wheel back the other way.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: What three-part sequence recovers a skidding vehicle cleanly back into its lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: In a skid you stay off the brake, steer where you want to go, and then steer back the other way as the car straightens.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Why does the first snowfall of the season demand extra defensive alertness?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Be extra alert on the first day of snowfall, because people are not yet used to driving in snow.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Which four specific areas—along with the rest of your car—must be cleared of snow and ice before driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Before a winter drive, clear snow and ice from the whole vehicle, including every window, the lights, the side mirrors and the license plates.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Besides scraping all glass, which three exterior parts does Wisconsin explicitly tell you to brush clean?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Clearing snow and ice covers the lamps, side mirrors and license plates as well as every window.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What two basic adjustments define safe everyday winter driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: In winter, drive slowly and leave extra space ahead of your vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: What is Wisconsin's rule on using cruise control when pavement turns slick?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Do not use cruise control on slippery roads.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: Which headlight setting belongs on—and which stays off—in winter snow conditions?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: In winter conditions, turn on your headlights but do not use your high beams.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: At least how many feet behind a flashing snowplow must you stay in Wisconsin?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Stay at least two hundred feet back from a snowplow whose lights are flashing red, amber or green.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: What are Wisconsin's two headline winter numbers and light rules—one for your beams and one for snowplows?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Winter driving calls for headlights on but high beams off, while the snowplow rule is about distance: at least two hundred feet behind a plow with flashing lights.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: Which three flashing light colors on a snowplow trigger the two-hundred-foot following rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: The snowplow distance applies whether the plow's flashing lights are red, amber or green.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Which three slow or unpredictable hazards should you watch for on Wisconsin rural roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Rural roads bring special hazards such as slow tractors, farm equipment and livestock.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: Why might a tractor operator miss your car behind them, and what lights can towed farm gear lack?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Farmers may have trouble seeing or hearing other traffic, and their equipment may have no brake lights or turn signals.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: Why is whipping out to pass a slowing tractor near a field driveway risky?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: Farm machinery may lack brake lights and turn signals, so you cannot count on it signaling a stop or turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: What attitude does the handbook call for when stuck behind wide, slow farm equipment?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Be patient around farm equipment on the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: Who holds the legal right-of-way when livestock are crossing or walking beside a Wisconsin highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: You must yield the right-of-way to livestock on or beside the highway.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: Why must you keep off your horn near livestock, and what should you do instead?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Near livestock, do not honk, since it may frighten the animals; slow down and keep a safe distance instead.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: What three behaviors combine when you encounter livestock on or along a rural highway?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Livestock on or along the highway get the right-of-way, and you slow down and keep a safe distance rather than using the horn.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Below what age is it illegal to operate a farm tractor or self-propelled farm machine on a Wisconsin highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: No one younger than sixteen may drive a farm tractor or self-propelled farm machinery on a highway.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: How do alcohol, drugs, and other impairing substances interfere with your thinking and traffic judgment?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Alcohol, drugs and other substances change how you think and decide, making it hard to judge the distance, speed and movement of other vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Does Wisconsin's ban on drugged driving cover prescription medications and store-bought remedies too?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Driving under the influence of any drug is illegal, and that includes both prescription and over-the-counter drugs.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: What happens to a driver's likelihood of crashing when driving drunk or drugged?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Drunk or drugged drivers have a higher chance of being in a crash.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What is Wisconsin's legal alcohol concentration limit for any driver under age twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: For drivers under the age of twenty-one the legal alcohol concentration is zero point zero zero percent, so they may not have any alcohol in their system while driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: How much of a controlled substance in your body counts legally as impaired driving in Wisconsin?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Having any amount of a controlled substance in your system counts the same as driving impaired.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: Who is bound by the zero-alcohol rule compared with Wisconsin's zero-tolerance rule for controlled substances?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: The zero point zero zero percent alcohol limit is the rule for drivers under twenty-one, while for controlled substances any amount counts as impaired regardless of the driver's age.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: According to research cited in the Wisconsin handbook, how does marijuana use affect driving performance?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Studies cited by the handbook show that marijuana users make more mistakes while driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: What must you check before getting behind the wheel after taking a prescription or nonprescription medicine?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Before driving after taking a prescription or over-the-counter medicine, read the warning label for side effects.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: When a medication bottle warns against operating heavy machinery, what everyday activity is included?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: A medicine label that warns against operating heavy machinery applies to driving a motor vehicle too.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Why doesn't having a doctor's prescription or store receipt make an impairing medicine legal to drive on?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: A medicine being legal to buy or prescribed to you does not make it legal to drive on, since driving under the influence of any drug is illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Which safe ride options does the Wisconsin handbook recommend if you have been drinking?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: If you have been drinking, get a ride home from a sober friend or relative, or ask a bartender to call a cab.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What is the single thing capable of sobering a person up after drinking alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Only time sobers a person up.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: Under Wisconsin's Implied Consent Law, how must you respond when an officer requests a PAC screening?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Under the implied consent law, when an officer requests a prohibited alcohol concentration (PAC) test, you are required to agree to it.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What does a prohibited alcohol concentration check look for, and which two methods does it use?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: A PAC test uses a breathalyzer or a blood test to find out whether you have a measurable amount of alcohol.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: Which two specimen methods can make up a prohibited alcohol concentration check in Wisconsin?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: A PAC test can be either a breathalyzer test or a blood test.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: What immediate action must a law enforcement officer take if you refuse a requested PAC test?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: If you refuse a PAC test, the officer must arrest you for violating the Implied Consent Law.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: For at least how long do you lose driving privileges after refusing a PAC test?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Refusing a PAC test costs you your driving privileges for at least one year, along with other consequences.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Why doesn't refusing an officer's PAC request work as a loophole to dodge trouble?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Refusing a PAC test leads to arrest under the Implied Consent Law and a loss of driving privileges for at least one year, so refusal is not a way out.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Because distraction is dangerous, what should hold your mental focus and your gaze while driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Distraction is dangerous, so concentrate on the driving task and keep your eyes on the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: What headphone or headset setup must you never wear while driving in Wisconsin?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Do not drive wearing headsets or headphones that cover or sit in both ears.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: What real-world sound benchmark sets how loud you may play your car radio?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Keep the radio volume low enough that you can hear emergency vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: Contrast what Wisconsin restricts on headsets versus how it regulates your car stereo?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: The headphone rule covers headsets or headphones that cover or go in both ears, and the radio rule is about keeping the volume low enough to hear emergency vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: How should you handle an incoming phone call while driving, and what if taking it is unavoidable?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Avoid answering your phone while driving; if you need it, pull over safely first.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Instead of picking up a ringing phone in moving traffic, what safe alternative does the handbook give?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Answering a phone is something to avoid while moving; the handbook's alternative is to pull over safely before using it.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Under what single circumstance may an instruction permit or probationary license holder use a cell phone while driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Instruction permit and probationary license holders may use a cell phone while driving only to report an emergency.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: What phone habit does the handbook urge for regular license holders, and how should necessary calls be placed?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Regular license holders should still avoid cell phones while driving and use the vehicle's hands-free option if a call is necessary.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: How do cell phone rules while driving compare between permit or probationary drivers and regular license holders?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Permit and probationary license holders may use a phone while driving only to report an emergency, while regular license holders are told to avoid it and use hands-free if they must.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: Where must your vehicle be before you read route directions or eat food?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Pull over to a safe place if you need to read directions, and eat only when the car is parked.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: Which two ways does the Wisconsin handbook recommend keeping a pet secure inside your car?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Keep pets in a carrier or have a passenger hold them.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: What two visibility-blocking decorations should you keep off your rearview mirror and vehicle windows?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Do not hang objects from the rearview mirror or cover your windows with decals.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: What rule links reading directions with eating a meal during a road trip?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Reading directions and eating are both tasks for a parked or pulled-over car, not for driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: What defines drowsy driving, and what causes it besides getting too little sleep?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: Drowsy driving means driving while very tired from too little sleep, which can also come from an untreated sleep disorder or a long work shift.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: Even after spending hours in bed, which two factors can still leave a driver dangerously drowsy?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Drowsiness can come from an untreated sleep disorder or a long work shift, not only from a short night's sleep.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: Why is getting a full night's sleep before driving especially critical for teens and young adults?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Get a good night's sleep before driving, since teen and young adult drivers face a higher risk of drowsiness-related crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: Which three physical or lane-keeping warning signs mean you must pull over and rest immediately?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Pull over and rest if you keep yawning or blinking, drift out of your lane, or hit the rumble strip at the road's edge.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: How should you treat drifting from your lane or striking the roadside rumble strip?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Drifting from your lane and hitting the rumble strip are drowsiness warning signs that call for pulling over to rest, just like frequent yawning or blinking.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: What safety advantage do you gain by keeping wider distance from other road users?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: The more distance you keep between yourself and other road users, the more time you have to react.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: On a multi-lane road, how should you adjust speed instead of cruising right beside another vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: On multi-lane roads, avoid riding right beside another driver; move ahead of the vehicle or drop back.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: How should you position your car near curbside parked vehicles and around blocked driver sightlines?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Give parked vehicles along the road extra room, and avoid lingering where another driver's view of you is blocked.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: Which two multi-lane positions should you avoid, and what single speed adjustment solves both?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: On multi-lane roads you avoid both riding right beside another driver and sitting where that driver cannot see you; moving ahead or dropping back fixes both.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Which people near traffic need extra alertness and wider space buffers from drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Stay alert for children and others who may run into the road without looking, and give extra room to pedestrians, confused drivers and anyone who cannot see you.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Under Wisconsin law, what is the single legal exception to the ban on driving across a sidewalk?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Driving on a sidewalk is illegal except to cross it.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and sirens?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: When you see emergency lights and hear sirens, move to the roadside and stay stopped there until the emergency vehicle has gone by.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Where must you never come to a stop when an emergency vehicle approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Never stop in the middle of an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: Contrast where yielding to an approaching emergency vehicle puts your car versus where you must never stop?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Pulling over for an emergency vehicle means going to the side of the road, never stopping inside an intersection.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: Which lane must you choose and hold when passing a stopped emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, move into a lane that is not next to it and stay in the farthest lane until you have passed it.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: How does your legal duty change between a moving emergency vehicle and one stopped with flashing lights?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: A moving emergency vehicle with lights and sirens means pull over and stop, while a stopped one with flashing lights means change to a lane away from it as you pass.
