sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What does Wisconsin law require when passing a police car stopped at the roadside with lights and siren active?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: When a police car is stopped on the roadside with lights and siren on, the law requires you to move over or slow down to give the officers room.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Which two legal options protect officers when a squad car sits stopped on the roadside?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: For a police car stopped on the roadside, the law gives two choices, move over or slow down, so that officers have room.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: At least how many feet away must you stop when a school bus flashes its red lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, stop at least twenty feet away from it.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: On an undivided roadway, which directions of traffic must stop for a school bus flashing red lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights whether it is on your side of the road or the opposite side.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: After stopping for a school bus, what must you watch for and when may you move again?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Watch for children around a stopped school bus, and go only after its red lights stop flashing.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Pair the minimum stopping gap for a flashing school bus with the exact cue allowing you to proceed?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: The school bus stop distance is at least twenty feet, and the signal that you may go again is the red lights no longer flashing.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: When are oncoming drivers exempt from stopping for a school bus on the opposite side of the highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: On a divided highway, where a barrier separates the opposing lanes, you need not stop for a school bus on the other side.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: Contrast who stops for a flashing school bus on an ordinary two-way street versus a barrier-divided highway?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: On an ordinary two-way road you stop for a flashing school bus on either side, but on a divided highway with a barrier you stop only if you are on the bus's side.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: Why must you leave extra following distance behind a motorcycle?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Motorcycles are lightweight and can stop faster than most vehicles, so give them extra room, especially when following one.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: What weight-related braking trait explains why motorcycles need extra following space?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Motorcycles need extra following room because, being lightweight, they can stop faster than most vehicles.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: What precautions should you take before changing lanes or passing around a motorcycle?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Around motorcycles, be extra aware and check your blind spots before moving, and wait until it is safe to pass.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: How much of a traffic lane is a bicyclist entitled to use, and may you squeeze alongside in that lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: A bicyclist may use the whole traffic lane, and you should not share a lane with one.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Why must you wait until oncoming traffic clears before overtaking a bicyclist?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Bicyclists can move into your path quickly and without warning, so wait for oncoming traffic to clear before you pass one.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: What minimum side clearance must you leave between your vehicle and a bicyclist when passing?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Leave at least three feet between your vehicle and a bicyclist when passing.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: Which two conditions—side space and opposing lane status—must line up before you pass a bicyclist?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: The passing gap for a bicyclist is at least three feet, and you also wait for oncoming traffic to clear before passing.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Why must drivers stay extra watchful for bicycles even though bikes are supposed to carry lights or reflectors?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Bicycles should carry reflectors or lights, but some do not, so stay watchful around them.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: What are truck no-zones, and roughly how far do they stretch behind and ahead of a large truck?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: No-zones are the areas around large vehicles where the driver cannot see you, reaching about two hundred feet behind and twenty feet in front of a large truck.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: How does the length of a large truck's rear no-zone compare with its front no-zone?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: The truck no-zone behind is about two hundred feet, far longer than the roughly twenty-foot no-zone in front.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: In which close-in fore-and-aft spots around a big truck does your car disappear from the trucker's view?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: Big trucks cannot see cars that are close behind them or right in front of them.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: How should you clear out of a truck's no-zone, and how should you handle passing one?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: If you are in a truck's no-zone, either speed up or drop back so the driver can see you, and when passing, get through the blind spot quickly.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: Pair the two ways to exit a truck's no-zone with the right pace when overtaking a rig?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Getting out of a truck's no-zone can mean speeding up or dropping back, and passing should take you through its blind spot quickly.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Whenever an emergency leaves you or someone else injured, what is always step number one?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: In any emergency where you or someone else is hurt, the first step is to call nine one one.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Are most traffic crashes unavoidable bad luck, or what habit lets you pick the right escape?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Most crashes can be avoided, and paying close attention to your surroundings helps you choose the right way to avoid one.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: How much does a teen driver's crash risk jump when just one other teenager rides along?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: A teen driver's chance of a crash doubles when another teen is riding in the vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: How should you alert trailing drivers when you spot a vehicle stopped along the side of the road ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: When you spot a vehicle on the side of the road, warn drivers behind you by tapping your brake pedal three or four times.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Why do you tap the brake pedal three or four times near a roadside vehicle instead of holding hard pressure?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Tapping the brake three or four times is a warning signal to drivers behind you, not an emergency stopping method.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: Which three maneuvers does the Wisconsin handbook give for avoiding an imminent crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: The handbook gives three ways to try to avoid a crash: stop, turn or speed up.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: How do you brake for an emergency stop in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: To stop fast with ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and keep steady pressure until you have stopped or the danger is over.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What mechanical problem does ABS prevent during hard braking, and what is the result?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: ABS keeps the wheels from locking when you brake, so you can stop with little or no skidding.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: Why is pumping the brake pedal wrong during an emergency stop in an ABS-equipped car?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Emergency braking with ABS uses firm, continuous pressure, not repeated pumping of the pedal.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: What collision hazard comes with making a sudden hard stop, and what habit guards against it?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Stopping quickly can lead a driver behind you to crash into you, so keep track of the vehicles behind.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: How should you grip the wheel when swerving around a hazard, and what trap hits right afterward?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: If you turn to avoid a crash, hold the wheel firmly with both hands and be ready to keep control afterward, since some drivers dodge one collision only to cause another.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Why is clearing the initial obstacle only half the battle when you turn to avoid a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: Turning away from one collision is only half the job, because you must then keep control so you do not cause a second one.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Where should your eyes and steering aim during an emergency dodge, and which lane is strictly off-limits?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: When steering away from danger, always steer where you want the vehicle to go and never into the oncoming lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: In which two impact angles can hitting the gas beat hitting the brakes, and what do you do once clear?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Speeding up can be the best escape when another vehicle is about to strike your car from the side or the rear, and you slow down again once the danger has passed.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: After accelerating ahead of a side or rear collision threat, what step completes the maneuver?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: The handbook example for speeding up is a vehicle about to strike your car from the side or the rear, and you slow down again once that danger has passed.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: After a collision before responders arrive, what must you do about leaving and alerting oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: If you are involved in a crash, or emergency help has not yet arrived, stay at the scene and warn other drivers with your emergency flashers or flares.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: When a crash injures or kills someone, what three rules govern nine-one-one, vehicle positions, and where you wait?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: If someone is injured or killed, call nine one one, stay at the scene without moving the vehicles, and stay inside your vehicle if that is safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: How does Wisconsin law treat driving away from a crash where someone was injured or killed?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Leaving the scene of a crash in which someone is injured or killed is a crime.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: If nobody is hurt in a crash yet your car won't drive, what three steps keep you safe?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: If no one is hurt but your vehicle cannot be moved, call nine one one, follow the dispatcher's directions and stay away from traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: When nobody is injured and your vehicle still drives safely after a minor crash, where do the cars belong?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: If no one is hurt and your vehicle can move, drive it off the road when safe rather than blocking traffic or stopping in the middle of the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: In a zero-injury collision, how does your next step differ between a disabled car and a drivable one?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: With no injuries but a car that cannot move, you call nine one one, follow the directions given and stay away from traffic, whereas a drivable car is moved off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: When do you leave crashed vehicles untouched in the road versus moving them to the side?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: With an injury or death you leave the vehicles where they are, but with no injuries and a drivable car you move it off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Which three categories of details must you exchange with other drivers after a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: After a crash, collect each other driver's license, vehicle and insurance information.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: Beyond driver documents, what three scene facts should you write down before memories fade?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Also record the damage to every vehicle, write down how the crash happened and get contact information from any witnesses.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Does any crash involving injury or death require a police report in Wisconsin?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: A crash must be reported to police whenever someone is injured or killed.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: At what dollar amount of general property damage must a Wisconsin crash be reported to police?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: A crash must be reported to police when property damage reaches one thousand dollars or more.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: At what lower dollar threshold must you report crash damage to government property like signs or guardrails?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: A crash must be reported to police when damage to government property, such as signs or guardrails, reaches two hundred dollars or more.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: How does Wisconsin's general property-damage reporting threshold compare with its government-property threshold?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.memory_hook: One thousand general, two hundred public
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: The police reporting threshold is one thousand dollars for property damage in general but only two hundred dollars for damage to government property such as signs or guardrails.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: Besides injury and dollar damage, which two scene conditions legally require reporting a crash to police?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: A crash must also be reported to police when your vehicle cannot be moved or a driver seems to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: When must you still report a crash to police even with zero injuries and minor visible damage?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: A crash needs a police report even without injuries or major damage when a vehicle cannot be moved or a driver appears impaired.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: What are your first two safety actions in any roadside emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: In a roadside emergency, call nine one one if anyone is injured and turn on your emergency flashers.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: Which two controls do you work—and in what order—if your regular brakes suddenly fail?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: If your brakes stop working, pump the brake pedal several times and then pull the parking brake.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: While slowing with the parking brake after brake failure, what must you do if the car starts skidding?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: If using the parking brake starts a skid, release it, and look for a safe place to slow to a stop.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: What is the complete three-part rule for handling failed brakes without spinning out?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: When the brakes fail, pumping the pedal comes first and the parking brake second, and the parking brake is released if it causes a skid.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: Which four calm steps bring your car safely off the road after a sudden tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: After a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel to keep going straight, lift your foot off the gas, slow down gradually and pull off the road when safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: If your engine quits while rolling, what do you do with the ignition key and what steering change will you feel?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: If the engine quits, hold the wheel, leave the key in the on position and pull to the side when safe, expecting the steering to be hard to turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: Why does steering suddenly take much more arm strength right after an engine stalls?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: The handbook warns that the steering wheel will be hard to turn after the engine stops, so expect extra effort while pulling over.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What switch check and backup lights help you pull off safely if your headlights go out?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: If your headlights stop working, try switching them off and on in case only the parking lights were on, turn on the emergency flashers and pull off the road when safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: What four-step sequence stops a vehicle safely when the gas pedal sticks down?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: If the gas pedal sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift into neutral, pull off the road when safe and then turn off the engine.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: Why do you leave the key in On during a stalled engine and wait until parked off-road to turn off a stuck-gas engine?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: When the engine dies you keep the key in the on position, and only with a stuck gas pedal does the handbook say to turn the engine off, once you are safely off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: How does your first move for a stuck gas pedal differ from your first move for a tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: A stuck gas pedal is handled by shifting into neutral, while a blowout is handled by easing off the gas and slowing gradually.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What credential is required to drive on Wisconsin public roads, and which four tests lead to it?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: You need a valid driver license to drive on any Wisconsin public road, and getting one means passing a short series of tests: a vision screening, a highway signs test, a knowledge test and a skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: What does Wisconsin's vision screening measure, and which two providers may conduct it?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: The vision screening measures how well you see, and either the DMV or your own vision specialist can give it.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: What minimum visual acuity score applies to regular car and motorcycle applicants, and are lenses permitted?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Regular car and motorcycle applicants must have visual acuity of at least twenty over forty in one eye, and glasses or contacts are allowed for that reading.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: How many degrees of side vision must Wisconsin applicants show, and from where is it measured?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Applicants must also have a seventy-degree field of vision measured from the center of each eye.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How do Wisconsin's twenty-over-forty acuity standard and seventy-degree field standard differ in eye coverage?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The acuity rule of at least twenty over forty needs to be met in only one eye, but the seventy-degree field-of-vision rule is measured from the center of each eye.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: Does needing prescription glasses or contacts to hit twenty over forty count against you during screening?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The twenty over forty acuity standard may be met with or without corrective lenses, so wearing glasses does not by itself fail the screening.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Which three functional categories of road signs does Wisconsin's highway signs test evaluate?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: The highway signs test checks whether you can read and understand the signs that regulate traffic, warn drivers and give directions.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: How many questions appear on Wisconsin's highway signs test, and what score passes it?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: The highway signs test has fifteen questions, and you must answer twelve of them correctly, which is eighty percent, to pass.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Must you reserve an appointment ahead of time to take Wisconsin's highway signs test?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: You can walk in for the highway signs test without making an appointment.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: How much of the Wisconsin handbook's sign coverage does the DMV advise studying beforehand?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: The handbook covers every type of sign you may meet, and it tells applicants to study all of them before the signs test.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What subject does Wisconsin's knowledge test measure, and is an advance appointment required?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: The knowledge test measures what you know about Wisconsin traffic laws, and you can take it without an appointment.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: How many total questions make up Wisconsin's knowledge test, and how many right answers pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: The knowledge test has fifty questions, and you need forty correct answers, or eighty percent, to pass.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: What passing percentage links Wisconsin's two written tests, and how do their raw numbers differ?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: Both written tests use the same eighty percent bar, but the highway signs test is twelve right out of fifteen while the knowledge test is forty right out of fifty.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How does the focus of Wisconsin's highway signs test differ from the focus of its knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: The highway signs test is about reading signs that regulate, warn and direct traffic, while the knowledge test is about traffic laws.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Roughly how long does Wisconsin's knowledge test take, and when must you arrive before closing?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Expect the knowledge test to take about forty-five minutes, so arrive early enough to finish before the DMV customer service center closes for the day.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: Why does the Wisconsin handbook remind walk-in applicants not to start the knowledge test late in the afternoon?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: Because the knowledge test takes about forty-five minutes, the handbook says to start early enough to finish before the customer service center closes.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What is the fee to take written tests at a Wisconsin DMV service center, and where can you practice free?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Taking the tests at a DMV customer service center is free, and the DMV website also offers a free practice test.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Which age group may take Wisconsin's knowledge test online from home, and what fee applies?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.memory_hook: Ages fifteen to seventeen, ten dollars
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Applicants between ages fifteen and seventeen have the option of taking the knowledge test online instead, for a fee of ten dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Contrast the cost of taking Wisconsin's written tests in person at a DMV center versus online?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The signs and knowledge tests are free at a DMV customer service center, while the online knowledge test option for ages fifteen to seventeen costs ten dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Can adult applicants aged eighteen and up use the paid online knowledge test described in the handbook?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: The handbook mentions the online knowledge test option only for applicants between ages fifteen and seventeen, and that option carries a fee.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: What other names refer to the skills test, and what basic ability does it prove behind the wheel?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: The skills test is the same thing as the road test or driving test: a real-world demonstration that you can keep ordinary, reasonable control of your vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: Which three terms does Wisconsin use interchangeably for the in-car exam with a DMV examiner?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: The road test, the driving test and the skills test are three names for the same on-road exam with a DMV examiner.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Who rides beside you during the skills test, and how do they guide your route and maneuvers?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: A DMV examiner goes with you on the skills test and gives spoken directions, for example to turn left at the next intersection or to make a Y-turn.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: How does booking the Wisconsin skills test differ from walking in for the written tests?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Unlike the written tests, the skills test needs an appointment, which you book through the road test page of the Wisconsin DMV website.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: Group Wisconsin's signs, knowledge, and skills tests by which allow walk-ins versus require online booking?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: The two written tests are walk-in, but the skills test is appointment-only and is scheduled on the DMV road test web page.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What six vehicle items does the DMV examiner inspect before your skills test leaves the lot?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.memory_hook: Horn, lights, signals, plates, doors, mirrors
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Before the skills test starts, the examiner inspects your car to confirm it is safe to drive, looking at the horn, lights and signals, license plates, doors, mirrors and more.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: Why can an applicant who practiced every driving maneuver still get turned away before starting the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: The examiner checks the car before any driving starts, looking at the horn, lights and signals, plates, doors and mirrors to make sure it is safe to drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: Which three cabin visibility controls does the handbook say you should know how to work effortlessly?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: You should know how to work every vehicle control you might need during the test, such as the headlights, the wipers and the defroster.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Why should you locate the headlight, wiper, and defrost switches before starting a road test in a borrowed car?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: Knowing where the headlight, wiper and defrost controls are is part of being ready for the road test, not an optional extra.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Along with turning, which two contrasting kinds of intersections are graded during Wisconsin's skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: The skills test grades turning, intersections where you must stop, and the approach to intersections where no stop is required.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: Do Wisconsin examiners grade only intersections with stop signs and red lights, or through approaches too?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: Intersections are graded both ways on the road test: the ones where you must stop and the ones you approach without a stop.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: Beyond turns and intersections, what three traffic environments or movements are scored on the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: It also grades driving through business or residential areas, changing lanes, and backing up.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Which three specific low-speed maneuvers appear on Wisconsin's skills test and deserve advance practice?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: The test includes set maneuvers such as a Y-turn, a roadside stop and start, and parking, so practice each one beforehand.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: How is the Y-turn highlighted twice in Wisconsin's overview of the driving skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: A Y-turn appears both as an example examiner instruction and as one of the listed maneuvers, alongside the roadside stop and start and parking.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: Where can you read extra Wisconsin skills-test prep tips, and what rehearsal rule does the handbook stress?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: The DMV website has more guidance on preparing for the skills test, and the handbook advises practicing every listed skill before test day.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Which license class covers standard noncommercial driving of cars and light trucks in Wisconsin?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: The licenses described in this chapter are Class D, the non-commercial license for driving a car or light truck.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: Where do you apply for a Wisconsin license, and what documents prove your full name and birth date?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: You apply for a license in person at a DMV service center, bringing proof of your full name and date of birth, such as a U.S. birth certificate or passport.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Alongside name and birth date, what legal standing must you document, and which same item can cover it?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: You also bring proof of U.S. citizenship or legal status, and a birth certificate or passport can serve for that as well.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: How many Wisconsin residency documents must you present, what examples qualify, and what number is required?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Applicants must show two documents proving Wisconsin residence, such as a utility bill or a financial statement listing their name and Wisconsin address, and must provide a Social Security number.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Contrast how one birth certificate or passport works for birth and status against what Wisconsin residency requires?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.memory_hook: One covers status; address needs two
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The same birth certificate or passport can prove both your name and date of birth and your citizenship or legal status, but residence needs two separate Wisconsin address documents.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Which two common cards satisfy Wisconsin's proof-of-identity requirement at the DMV counter?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Proof of identity can be a signed Social Security card or a state-issued photo ID card, and showing the Social Security card also satisfies the identity requirement.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Why are photocopies or expired IDs turned away at the DMV, and what non-paperwork standards apply?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Every document must be valid, so photocopies and expired items are not accepted, and applicants must also meet physical and medical requirements.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Who must sign a minor's Wisconsin Driver License Application, and what form number is it?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen needs an adult sponsor to sign the Wisconsin Driver License Application, form MV3001.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What legal and financial responsibility does an adult sponsor take on, and can they cancel it later?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: A sponsor accepts liability, which means being legally and financially responsible for incidents the minor causes while driving, and the sponsor can withdraw sponsorship at any time.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: What school-standing facts does a sponsor certify upfront, and what driving record do they sign off on later?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: The sponsor confirms that the applicant under eighteen is enrolled in school and is not habitually truant, and later verifies the teen's practice driving hours.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Through what license stage and until what birthday does adult sponsorship remain active?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Sponsorship continues through the probationary phase until the driver turns eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which four household or exchange-program adults qualify to sponsor a teen living with family?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: A parent, step-parent or legal guardian may sponsor a teen, and so may the sponsoring parent of a foreign exchange student.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: When a minor lives apart from parents or guardians, which six relatives or foster adults may sponsor?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: When the teen does not live with a parent or legal guardian, a grandparent, aunt or uncle, foster parent, or a sibling or spouse who is eighteen or older may sign as sponsor.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Among extended-family sponsors, which two must be at least eighteen while the others carry no stated age floor?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: A sibling or spouse may sponsor only if they are eighteen or older, but a grandparent, aunt, uncle or foster parent has no stated age condition.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Which independent or bereaved minors may file proof of insurance in place of an adult sponsor?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Some applicants under eighteen file proof of insurance in place of a sponsor, including those with no living parent and those who live apart from their parents while studying full time or earning a living.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Which two additional groups of minors can substitute proof of insurance for an adult sponsor?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: Proof of insurance also replaces a sponsor for a minor who is a ward of the state, county or court placed in foster or religious welfare care, or who is married to a spouse under eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Contrast replacing a sponsor through proof of insurance against using an extended-family relative as sponsor?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Proof of insurance replaces a sponsor for certain minors, such as one with no living parent, whereas a listed relative may sponsor a teen who is not living with a parent or legal guardian.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Why must beginners get an instruction permit first, and which three checks qualify an applicant eighteen or older?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: You need an instruction permit to practice driving before the road test, and an applicant eighteen or older qualifies by passing the knowledge test, the highway signs test and the vision screening.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Beyond passing vision, signs, and knowledge, what age floor and course rule apply to permit seekers under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen must also be at least fifteen and enrolled in driver education, including its behind-the-wheel portion.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: What separates the instruction-permit requirements for someone under eighteen from someone eighteen or older?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Adults eighteen and older can get a permit by passing the knowledge test, signs test and vision screening, while teens also need to be at least fifteen and enrolled in driver education.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What signed form must a teen's behind-the-wheel driving school provide before the teen applies for a permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: The behind-the-wheel school gives the teen a signed MV3001 application, which must be completed before applying for the permit.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Which two separate parties sign form MV3001 along a Wisconsin teen's path to an instruction permit?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: A sponsor signs form MV3001 for an applicant under eighteen, and the behind-the-wheel school also supplies a signed MV3001, so the same form number appears twice in the teen path.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: May a Class D permit holder ever drive solo, and what license status and experience must their mentor have?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A Class D permit holder may never drive alone; the companion must have at least two years of licensed driving experience and a valid regular license, not a probationary or occupational one.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Why do probationary and occupational licenses fail to qualify someone to supervise a Wisconsin permit driver?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: Every permit companion needs at least two years of licensed experience on a valid regular license; a probationary or occupational license does not qualify.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: Where must the supervising companion sit, and what minimum ages apply across instructors, family, and others?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: That companion sits in the front passenger seat and must be a qualified instructor aged nineteen or older, a parent, guardian or spouse aged nineteen or older, or any person aged twenty-one or older.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: Which supervising companions qualify at age nineteen on a permit, and who must be at least twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: On a permit, a qualified instructor or a parent, guardian or spouse must be at least nineteen, but any other companion must be at least twenty-one.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Under what front-seat supervision condition may a permit driver carry immediate family in the back seat?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: When a parent, guardian or spouse is the companion, immediate family members of the permit holder may also ride in the back seat.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Before a minor permit holder drives with a qualified adult aged twenty-one or older, what consent is required?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: If the permit holder is under eighteen, a companion aged twenty-one or older needs written permission from the minor's parent or guardian before the drive begins.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Once a permit holder is sixteen, what single extra non-family passenger may ride in a rear seat?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: A permit holder aged at least sixteen may carry one more licensed person, aged twenty-five or older with at least two years of driving experience, in a seat other than the front seat.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Compare the youngest possible age of a front-seat permit mentor with an extra licensed rider in back?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: The extra back-seat licensed passenger allowed on a permit must be at least twenty-five, whereas the front-seat companion can be as young as nineteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: Who must sit in the front passenger seat whenever a permit holder practices driving in darkness?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Driving in darkness on a permit requires either a qualified instructor or a licensed person aged twenty-five with at least two years of licensed experience in the seat beside you.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: Which Wisconsin license is issued right after passing the skills test, and what is its minimum age?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: The probationary license is the first license issued after you pass the skills test, and you must be at least sixteen to receive it.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Under what sole exception may someone driving on a Wisconsin probationary license use a phone?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Phones may not be used while driving on a probationary license except to report an emergency.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: What permit tenure, birthday, and course proof must an applicant under eighteen have before getting a probationary license?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen must hold the instruction permit for at least six months, be sixteen, and prove completion of driver education before getting the probationary license.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: Why is turning sixteen by itself not enough to qualify a teen for a Wisconsin probationary license?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: Before a probationary license, a teen needs six months on the permit, a sixteenth birthday and proof of driver education, so turning sixteen alone is not enough.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: How many supervised practice hours must a permit holder log, and how do day and dark hours divide?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.memory_hook: Fifty hours; forty day, ten dark
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: Supervised practice on the permit must total at least fifty hours, made up of forty daytime hours and ten hours in darkness, with a qualified adult.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Can fifty hours of bright-daylight driving satisfy Wisconsin's supervised permit practice rule?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Permit practice needs forty daytime hours and ten darkness hours, so the fifty-hour total cannot be met with daytime driving alone.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: Is fifty hours a cap or a floor, and who verifies both the total and after-dark hours?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Fifty hours is only the minimum, more may be needed to show safe driving, and the sponsor must verify the full fifty hours including the ten after dark.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Which two tools can Wisconsin sponsors use to record a teen's supervised practice hours?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: Sponsors can print a driving log or use the RoadReady mobile app to track practice hours.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: What is another name for a teen probationary license, who faces its limits, and why?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: The probationary license is also called a graduated driver license, or GDL, and its passenger and hour limits apply to drivers under eighteen to cut distractions.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: How long do initial GDL passenger and curfew restrictions last, and is a new card needed afterward?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: The GDL limits last for the first nine months unless the driver turns eighteen sooner, and no new license is needed when they end.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: From five a.m. to midnight, where may a GDL teen drive solo and how many immediate family members may ride?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Between five a.m. and twelve a.m., a GDL driver may drive alone anywhere and may carry any number of immediate family members.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: From five a.m. to midnight, which non-family passengers may ride with a GDL driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: Between five a.m. and twelve a.m., a GDL driver may also carry one other passenger plus one licensed adult with at least two years of experience who is a qualified instructor or spouse aged nineteen or older, or anyone aged twenty-one or older.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: Contrast how daytime GDL passenger limits treat immediate family members versus non-family peers?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: Immediate family members are unlimited as passengers during the daytime GDL window, while other riders are limited to one qualifying licensed adult plus one other person.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: Between midnight and five a.m., between which three destinations may a GDL teen drive solo?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Between twelve a.m. and five a.m., a GDL driver may drive alone only when traveling between home, school and work.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: What passenger limit applies to a GDL driver during the midnight-to-five-a.m. window?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: During those midnight-to-five a.m. hours the same passenger limit applies: one qualifying licensed adult with at least two years of experience plus one other person.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: How do solo GDL trip destinations change when the clock strikes midnight until five a.m.?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: In the five a.m. to twelve a.m. window a GDL driver may go anywhere alone, but in the twelve a.m. to five a.m. window driving alone is allowed only between home, school and work.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: Which three record events extend a teen's GDL restrictions, and by how many months?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: The GDL limits are extended by six months after a moving violation conviction, any breach of the limits, or a suspension or revocation for any reason.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: Compare the normal length of Wisconsin GDL restrictions with the length added after a violation?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: The GDL limits normally last nine months, but a moving violation, a breach of the limits or a suspension or revocation adds six more months.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: What happens to demerit points on a second or later traffic conviction while holding a permit or probationary license?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: The handbook says points on second or later convictions double during this phase, as with the permit, and enough points on your record can cost you the license.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: At what birthday do Wisconsin's GDL passenger and night-hour restrictions end completely?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: The GDL hour and passenger limits stop applying once the driver turns eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: What license stage follows Wisconsin's probationary license, and how early can you renew into it?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: The regular driver license is the final step after the probationary license, and renewal can begin ninety days before the probationary license expires.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: How often is a Wisconsin regular license renewed, how early may you renew, and where?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: A regular license must be renewed every eight years, renewal is allowed up to one year ahead of expiration, and it can be done online or at a service center.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.front: Compare how early you can renew a regular license against upgrading from probationary to regular?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.expected_back: Renewal of the regular license is every eight years and may be done up to one year early, while the probationary-to-regular renewal window opens ninety days before expiration.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.front: When does Wisconsin send out your driver license renewal reminder?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.expected_back: A renewal reminder arrives forty-five to sixty days before your birthday in the year your license expires.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.front: Within how many days of moving to Wisconsin should a new resident transfer an out-of-state regular license?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.expected_back: A new resident holding another state's regular license is an out-of-state transfer and should apply for a Wisconsin license within sixty days of moving.

sec02-card-sec02-F43.front: How soon after moving to Wisconsin must a commercial driver license holder apply for a Wisconsin CDL?
sec02-card-sec02-F43.expected_back: A commercial driver license holder from another state should apply for the Wisconsin CDL within thirty days of moving.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.front: Contrast Wisconsin's new-resident license transfer window for a regular license versus a commercial CDL?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.expected_back: A new resident has sixty days to apply for a Wisconsin regular license but only thirty days for a commercial license.

sec02-card-sec02-F44.front: If your old state license already had a REAL ID star, does that status transfer automatically to Wisconsin?
sec02-card-sec02-F44.expected_back: A REAL ID from your previous state does not carry over, so you must present all acceptable documents again to get a Wisconsin REAL ID.

sec02-card-sec02-F45.front: Whose federal standards does a REAL ID satisfy, and what symbol marks a compliant Wisconsin card?
sec02-card-sec02-F45.expected_back: A REAL ID meets U.S. Department of Homeland Security standards, and Wisconsin marks its REAL ID cards with a star.

sec02-card-sec02-F46.front: Starting May seven, two thousand twenty-five, which trips and facilities require a REAL ID or passport?
sec02-card-sec02-F46.expected_back: Beginning May seven, two thousand twenty-five, flying within the U.S. or entering a military base or other federal building requires REAL ID-compliant identification or another accepted ID such as a passport.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.front: What symbol marks a REAL ID license, and what common travel document works in its place for domestic flights?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.expected_back: A REAL ID card is marked with a star, and from May seven, two thousand twenty-five a passport is an accepted alternative for domestic flights and federal buildings.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Why does Wisconsin favor roundabouts, and which direction does traffic always travel inside one?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: The handbook presents roundabouts as a safer and more efficient way to move traffic, and traffic inside one always circulates counterclockwise.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: What guides your lane selection approaching a roundabout, and how do left, middle, and right lanes usually divide turns?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Overhead signs on the approach show which lane to use; generally the left lane is for left turns, the right lane for the next right, and the middle lane for going straight.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Before reaching the yield line of a roundabout, what speed change do you make and whom do you yield to first?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: As you approach a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians and bicycles.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: At the entrance to a roundabout, which direction of circulating traffic—and what large vehicle—must you yield to?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Before entering, yield to traffic coming from your left that is already in the roundabout, and yield to semitrucks.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: Which four road users get priority before you pull into a Wisconsin roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Before entering a roundabout you yield to pedestrians, bicycles, semitrucks and the traffic on your left that is already circulating.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: When do you pull into a roundabout, and must you come to a full stop if the circle is empty?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Enter only when there is a safe gap, and if the roundabout is empty you do not have to wait.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: How does your entry move change between a busy roundabout and a completely empty one?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: A safe gap is needed to enter a busy roundabout, but an empty roundabout may be entered without stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Which three speed and lane rules apply once your car is circulating inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.memory_hook: Low speed, hold lane, never switch
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Inside the roundabout keep your speed low, stay in your lane and never switch lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What blinker move tells waiting drivers you are about to leave the roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: When you near your exit, turn on your right turn signal and leave the roundabout.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Even if your overall route turned left through the roundabout, which turn signal marks your exit?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: The signal used to leave a roundabout is the right turn signal, given as you reach your exit.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: What should you do if an emergency vehicle running its siren enters a roundabout before you pull in?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: If an emergency vehicle with its siren on enters a roundabout before you do, pull over and let it go by instead of entering.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: If you are already inside a roundabout when an emergency vehicle approaches, why must you exit before pulling over?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: If you are already in the roundabout when an emergency vehicle comes, leave at the next right exit and then pull over, avoiding any stop inside the circle.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does yielding to a siren-lit responder change once you have already entered a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Outside the roundabout you pull over for an emergency vehicle, but inside it you first exit at the next right and only then pull over.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Which two legal options does a bicyclist have for navigating a one-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: At a one-lane roundabout a bicyclist may either ride through the roundabout or use the crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: At a roundabout crosswalk, which way do pedestrians look from the curb versus from the center island?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Pedestrians crossing at a roundabout look left for oncoming traffic from the curb and look right once they reach the crosswalk island.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: Why does a pedestrian's head check flip from left at the curb to right on the roundabout island?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: A pedestrian at the curb looks left for oncoming traffic, while a pedestrian on the crosswalk island looks right.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What two steps are critical before pulling into a two-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: At a two-lane roundabout your lane choice is critical: choose a lane and yield to traffic in both lanes before you enter.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: When entering the right lane of a two-lane roundabout, why isn't checking only the outside lane enough?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: At a two-lane roundabout you yield to traffic in both circulating lanes, not just the lane nearest you.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: In a two-lane roundabout, which lane handles left turns and U-turns, right turns, and going straight?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: In a two-lane roundabout, use the left lane for left turns and U-turns, the right lane for right turns, and follow the pavement markings, arrows or signs to go straight.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Why should you check pavement arrows and overhead boards when going straight through a two-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: At a two-lane roundabout, use the left lane for left turns or U-turns, use the right lane for right turns, and follow the pavement markings, arrows, or signs to go straight.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: How may a bicyclist pass through a two-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: A bicyclist at a two-lane roundabout may take the travel lane through it or leave the roadway and use the crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What is the purpose of traffic signals placed on freeway entrance ramps?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Some freeway on-ramps have traffic signals that space out merging vehicles, which eases congestion on both the freeway and the ramp.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: How can you tell as you enter an on-ramp whether its ramp meter signals are currently operating?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: A ramp is being metered when its Ramp Metered When Flashing sign is lit.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: Where must your front tires stop at an active ramp meter, and what happens if you stop short?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: At a metered ramp, pull all the way up to the white stop line so your tires set off the sensors in the pavement.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Why does the Wisconsin handbook emphasize pulling all the way up to a ramp meter's white stop line?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: At a ramp meter you pull all the way up to the white stop line because that is where your tires trigger the pavement sensors.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: On a two-lane metered on-ramp, how do the signals work and when do you merge?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Each ramp lane has its own signal, and you may go and merge into traffic once your signal turns green.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: What tells you a multi-lane ramp meter is running, and whose green light clears you to go?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Ramp meters operate only while the Ramp Metered When Flashing sign is lit, and then each lane waits for its own green.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Are ramp meter red lights optional suggestions, or what happens if you blow through one?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Disobeying a ramp meter signal can earn you a ticket.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: What three benefits does a diverging diamond interchange deliver, and how do you navigate it?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: A diverging diamond interchange routes drivers smoothly through exits and entrances to improve safety, reduce crowding and cut road costs; follow its signs, signals and markings.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: Why do highway engineers build diverging diamond interchanges, and what keeps drivers in the right spot?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: A diverging diamond interchange is meant to improve safety, reduce crowding and lower the cost of new roads, and drivers get through it by following its signs, signals and markings.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: What overarching goal guides law enforcement, and what three possibilities might an officer investigate during a stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Law enforcement's top priority is public safety, and during a stop the officer checks for a possible incident, crime or minor law violation.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: Which side of the roadway should you pull onto when patrol lights flash behind you?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: When you see emergency lights flashing behind you, pull off to the right side of the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: Right after pulling to the shoulder for a police stop, what three things do you do with your shifter, engine, and audio?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Once stopped, shift into park and turn off both the engine and the radio.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: During a traffic stop, what should you do regarding staying inside, your seat belt, and your window?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: During a traffic stop, stay inside the vehicle with your seat belt fastened and roll your window down.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: Should you step out of your car to walk back and meet the officer during a traffic stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: At a traffic stop you stay in the vehicle with your seat belt on, rather than getting out to meet the officer.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Where should you rest your hands during a traffic stop, and what movements should you avoid?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Keep your hands on top of the steering wheel where the officer can see them, and avoid sudden moves or reaching for things.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: If you think a traffic ticket is unfair, how should you act roadside and where do you make your case?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Do not argue if you get a ticket; you will have a chance to raise your concerns before a judge or court.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: What is the proper place to contest a traffic citation in Wisconsin?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: A ticket is contested before a judge or court, not by arguing with the officer at the roadside.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: During what daily window are deer most active along Wisconsin roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Deer are most active between sunset and sunrise.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: What visual clue gives away deer near dark roadsides, and what three actions should follow?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Scan for your headlights reflecting in a deer's eyes; if you see them, slow down, sound your horn and be ready to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: Why shouldn't you relax after one deer bounds clear, or assume city streets are deer-free?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Expect more than one deer, and remember they wander from rural areas into towns and cities and can cross at any place and time.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.front: Once you slow and honk for a deer's glowing eyes, why must you keep scanning after it clears?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.expected_back: Seeing a deer's eyes calls for slowing down and using the horn, and you keep watching because more deer may follow.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: If you hit a deer, what mechanical check comes first, and what details should you write down?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: After hitting a deer, first check that your vehicle is still safe to drive, then record the time, place and details for insurance and crash reports.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: Under Wisconsin rules, who gets first claim to keep a vehicle-struck deer, and who is second in line?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: A driver who hits a deer may keep it, and if that driver does not want it, the next motorist may keep it.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: Why must you phone police after striking a deer whether you keep it or leave it behind?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: Call the police after hitting a deer so they can issue a tag for it, and call them to say where it is if you do not want the deer.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.front: Does declining to keep a deer you hit excuse you from calling law enforcement?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.expected_back: The police issue the tag for a deer you hit, and you still call them to report its location even if you do not keep it.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: How does the Wisconsin handbook define a funeral procession?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: A funeral procession carries the deceased from a funeral home or place of worship to a cemetery or crematorium.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: In a Wisconsin funeral procession, what rule binds the first vehicle, and what must every vehicle in line turn on?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: The first vehicle in a funeral procession must obey traffic signs and signals, and every vehicle in the line must have its headlights on.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.front: Which requirement applies solely to the lead vehicle of a funeral procession versus every car in line?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.expected_back: In a funeral procession the lead vehicle must follow traffic signs and signals, and every vehicle in the line keeps its headlights on.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: What is the rule for outside drivers encountering a moving funeral procession?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: Never cut into a funeral procession or interfere with it.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: At what point total does every Wisconsin driving record begin, and what adds demerit points?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Every driving record starts at zero points, and being convicted of a traffic law violation can add demerit points.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Which three driver groups face doubled demerit points, and on which conviction does doubling start?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Drivers holding a probationary license, only an ID card, or no license at all have their points doubled on the second conviction and every one after it.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: Do probationary, ID-card, or unlicensed drivers get doubled points on their very first traffic conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Point doubling applies to probationary license holders, ID card holders and unlicensed drivers, and starts with the second conviction rather than the first.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Accumulating how many demerit points within what rolling timeframe suspends or revokes your driving privilege?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Collecting twelve or more demerit points within any twelve-month period leads to suspension or revocation of your driving privilege.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: What five-year conviction totals—major or minor—classify a driver as a habitual traffic offender?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: You become a habitual traffic offender with four or more major traffic violation convictions, or twelve or more minor ones, within five years.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How does Wisconsin's twelve-point loss rule differ from habitual-offender status in both unit counted and timeframe?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: The twelve-point rule counts demerit points within any twelve-month period, while the habitual offender rule counts convictions over five years.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Within a five-year span, compare how many major convictions versus minor convictions trigger habitual-offender status?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Habitual offender status takes only four major violations but twelve minor ones within five years.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Where can you check exact demerit point values and see whether an offense counts as major or minor?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: The DMV website lists the points for each violation and which violations count as major or minor.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: How long is a habitual traffic offender's privilege revoked, and how long before occupational eligibility may open?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: A habitual traffic offender's driving privilege is revoked for five years, with possible eligibility for an occupational license after a two-year wait.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: For a habitual traffic offender, contrast the full revocation term against the waiting period for a possible occupational license?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: For a habitual traffic offender the revocation lasts five years, but an occupational license may become possible after a two-year wait.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Which five actions can take away your Wisconsin driving privilege, and must you hold a Wisconsin license first?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Your Wisconsin driving privilege can be lost through suspension, revocation, cancellation, disqualification or denial, even if you do not hold a Wisconsin license.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: Before applying for an occupational license, what should you check online and what proof must you present?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: To apply for an occupational license, first check your eligibility on the DMV website; you will need to show proof of financial responsibility.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: What daily and weekly driving-hour ceilings govern a Wisconsin occupational license?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: An occupational license caps your driving at twelve hours per day and sixty hours per week.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: Can driving twelve hours every day of the week stay legal under an occupational license?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: The occupational license caps are twelve hours in a day and sixty hours in a week, and both apply at once.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Which everyday destinations—including two household examples—are permitted on an occupational license?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Occupational license driving is limited to trips to and from work, school and places needed to maintain your household, such as the grocery store and medical appointments.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: Beyond work, school, and household errands, which assessment and safety-plan trips does an occupational license cover?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: An occupational license also covers trips to the agency handling your Intoxicated Driver Program (IDP) assessment and Driver Safety Plan (DSP).

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: Once your revocation term finishes, which three steps reinstate your Wisconsin driver license?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: A revoked license can be reinstated once the revocation period ends, by presenting proof of identity, paying a reinstatement fee and, if required, filing proof of financial responsibility.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: While both may require financial responsibility proof, which two items does the handbook list specifically for reinstating a revoked license?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Both getting an occupational license and reinstating a revoked one can require proof of financial responsibility, but only reinstatement adds a fee and proof of identity in the handbook.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: What format and language accommodations are offered for Wisconsin's knowledge and highway signs tests, and where are languages listed?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: The knowledge and signs tests can be taken with audio and in many languages, which are listed on the DMV website.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Which disclosure form and three delivery methods let you notify the DMV about an invisible disability?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.memory_hook: Disclosure form via email, mail, fax
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: You can tell the DMV about an invisible disability using the Invisible Disability Disclosure form MV2167, sent by email, mail or fax.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Which two groups of personnel have access to an invisible disability disclosure filed with Wisconsin?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: An invisible disability disclosure is made available to law enforcement officers and WisDOT employees.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What health conditions must you report to the DMV, and which standard license form lets you report them?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Report any health condition that could affect your driving to the DMV, which you can do on the Wisconsin Driver License Application MV3001.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How do the Wisconsin forms differ between reporting a driving-related medical condition and disclosing an invisible disability?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Medical conditions are reported on the driver license application MV3001, while an invisible disability is disclosed on the separate form MV2167.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: How can Wisconsin citizens missing standard paperwork obtain a free identification card for voting?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Wisconsin citizens can get a free ID card for voting through a petition process using the ID Application MV3004 and the Administrator Petition for unavailable documents MV3012.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: What practical benefit does the voting ID petition deliver before election day arrives?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Through the voting ID petition you receive a document you can use in time to vote.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: What minimum age and citizenship requirement must you meet to start Wisconsin's voting ID petition process?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: To start the voting ID petition process you must be at least seventeen years old and a U.S. citizen.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: Which five categories of available proof or personal info should you bring when starting a voting ID petition?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: For the voting ID petition, bring whatever you have of proof of name and birth date, proof of identity, Wisconsin residency, proof of U.S. citizenship and your Social Security number.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: Who must wear a seat belt inside a motor vehicle under Wisconsin law?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Wisconsin law requires the driver and all passengers of any age to wear seat belts.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Does Wisconsin's mandatory seat belt law let adult back-seat passengers ride unbuckled?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: The seat belt law covers passengers of any age, not just children or the driver.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: In what three ways does wearing a seat belt protect you while driving or during an impact?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Seat belts keep you positioned to control the vehicle, help prevent injury in a crash and help keep you from being thrown out.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: When should you fasten your seat belt, and what should you verify for everyone riding with you?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Buckle your seat belt before you start driving and make sure every passenger buckles up too.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Does driving a vehicle equipped with air bags excuse you from wearing a seat belt?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: You must still wear a seat belt in a vehicle that has air bags.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: Across which exact body areas should your lap belt and shoulder belt rest?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: The lap belt should sit snugly across your hip bones just below your stomach, and the shoulder belt should cross your chest.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: How much slack fits properly at your chest, and what two shoulder-belt positions are unsafe?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Adjust the belt so your fist fits between it and your chest, and never tuck the shoulder belt under your arm or let it hang loose over your arm.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: Contrast how the lap strap and the shoulder strap fit properly across your body?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: The lap belt goes low across the hip bones, while the shoulder belt crosses the chest with about a fist of room.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: Generally, until what ages do children ride in a child safety seat and then a booster seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Generally, children ride in a child safety seat until age four and in a booster seat until age eight.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Put Wisconsin's two general child-restraint stages in sequence along with each stage's age milestone?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: A child generally needs a child safety seat until age four and then a booster seat until age eight.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Where should you look to confirm proper belt routing and height-and-weight limits for a child safety seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Check the child safety seat's manual for how to fasten the seat belt and for its weight and height requirements.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: What type of auto insurance must you carry in Wisconsin, and when must you show proof?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: You must carry valid liability car insurance to drive in Wisconsin and show proof of it when a police officer asks.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: Who must issue a Wisconsin resident's policy, and what insurance proof may out-of-state visitors show?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: Your insurance must come from a business approved in Wisconsin, though drivers from another state may show proof from their own state's insurer.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: When you get behind the wheel of a friend's or relative's vehicle, whose job is verifying it has insurance?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: When you drive someone else's car, it is your responsibility to make sure that car is insured.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: Contrast Wisconsin's insurance rule for out-of-state motorists with the rule for driving someone else's car?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Out-of-state drivers may show proof of insurance from their home state's company, but anyone driving another person's car must still make sure it is insured.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Which travel choices and trip-timing habits help cut down on fuel consumption?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: You can save fuel by carpooling, ride sharing, biking, taking the bus or walking, and by avoiding heavy traffic periods.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: How does stop-and-go driving affect your car compared with easing off speed gradually?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Stop-and-go driving adds wear and tear, while slowing down gradually saves both fuel and brakes.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: What safety and cost risks come from poor vehicle upkeep, and how do underinflated tires hurt efficiency?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: A vehicle in poor condition costs more to run and could break down and crash, and low tire pressure lowers fuel mileage.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: What training costs can Wisconsin's Driver Education Grant Program cover for income-eligible teens?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: Under the Driver Education Grant Program, income-eligible teens can have their classroom training, behind-the-wheel training, or both paid for by the state.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: Do age or past medical conditions disqualify someone from registering as an organ and tissue donor?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: People of all ages can register as organ and tissue donors, regardless of their health history.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: Once you turn eighteen, can relatives override your organ donor registration, and why still talk with family?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: If you are eighteen or older, your organ donor decision cannot be overridden by your family or anyone else, so share your decision with your family.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: Even though an eighteen-year-old's donor choice cannot be overturned by relatives, what step does the handbook still urge?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: An adult donor's decision, from age eighteen, cannot be overridden by family, yet the handbook still advises telling your family.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: When an officer, school crossing guard, or road worker holds a traffic paddle that contradicts a light, whom must you obey?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: When a police officer, school crossing guard or other worker directs traffic with a sign, you must obey that person even if a traffic light or road sign says something different.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: What colors, usual outline, and safety purpose define standard roadway warning panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols, most are diamond shaped, and they alert you to a hazard or special situation ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: What roadway junction ahead is announced by an Intersection or Cross Road warning panel?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: An Intersection or Cross Road warning sign marks a spot ahead where two or more roads cross each other.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What physical change in opposing lanes does a Divided Highway panel announce ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: A Divided Highway sign means opposing lanes ahead will be separated by a physical barrier such as a guardrail.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: What road surface danger and driver adjustment are prompted by a Slippery When Wet panel?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: A Slippery When Wet sign means the pavement ahead may be slick, so reduce your speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What lies downstream of a Signal Ahead warning panel, and how should you prepare?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: A Signal Ahead sign warns of traffic lights ahead, so be prepared to slow and stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: What wildlife pattern does a Deer Crossing panel mark, and what mindset does it demand?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: A Deer Crossing sign marks an area where deer very often cross the road, so stay alert.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What does a Lane Ends warning panel reveal, and what maneuver should you execute?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: A Lane Ends sign shows which lane is ending; move into the remaining lane once it is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: What kind of alignment lies ahead of a Curved Road panel, and how much should you slow?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: A Curved Road sign warns that the road bends gradually right or left, and you slow only as much as needed to drive it safely.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How does a Sharp Turn warning panel differ in geometry and braking prep from a Curved Road panel?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: A Sharp Turn sign can point left or right and asks you to be ready to slow for the turn, unlike a Curved Road sign, which marks a gradual bend.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does the lane picture on a Merge panel contrast with a Lane Ends panel, and what action do both share?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: A Merge sign shows a lane joining from the right or left, while a Lane Ends sign shows your own lane ending; in both cases you move over when it is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: What terrain change does a Hill panel announce, and how should you respond?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: A Hill sign warns of a hill ahead, and you slow down if needed to stay safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: At what roadway transition is a Two-Way Traffic warning panel posted?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: A two-Way Traffic sign appears where a one-way road ends and you enter a road carrying traffic in both directions.
