sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: What two graphics appear on a Stop Ahead panel, and what action does it ask of you?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: A Stop Ahead sign shows an arrow with a stop-sign shape beneath it and tells you to slow so you can stop safely at the stop sign ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: How are the symbol and text plaque arranged on a Roundabout Ahead warning display?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: A Roundabout Ahead sign is a diamond with a counterclockwise symbol above a rectangular plaque reading Roundabout Ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What does the arrow plaque underneath a Pedestrian Crossing panel pinpoint, and what is your legal duty?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: A Pedestrian Crossing sign has an arrow plaque below the walker symbol showing where the crossing is, and you must yield to anyone crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Which two background colors are used on Wisconsin school zone and crossing panels, and what must you do there?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: School zone and school crossing signs may be fluorescent green or yellow, and you must yield to pedestrians crossing there.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: What do regulatory boards communicate, and what outlines, backgrounds, and letter colors do they use?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Regulatory signs state the rules of the road; they are square, rectangular or a special shape and white or red with black, red, white or green lettering.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What command does a Do Not Enter board give, and at what two wrong-way trouble spots is it mounted?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: A Do Not Enter sign means you may not go in; it is posted on one-way streets and on exit ramps facing the wrong direction.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: Under what roadway conditions does a posted Speed Limit board allow driving at its top number?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: A Speed Limit sign gives the highest speed allowed when driving conditions are good.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What adjustment does a Reduced Speed Ahead board call for, and why might it stand there?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: A Reduced Speed Ahead sign tells you to slow down, for example because a slippery road may lie ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: Which category does Reduced Speed Ahead belong to, and what two example hazards might prompt it?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Reduced Speed Ahead is a regulatory sign meaning you should slow down because a curb or slippery road might lie ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: When does the lower speed cap on a Wisconsin school zone speed limit board take effect?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: On a school zone speed limit sign, the posted speed may not be exceeded whenever children can be seen.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What physical feature sits in the roadway ahead when a Keep Right board appears?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: A Keep Right sign means a traffic island or other obstacle divides the road ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: How does a directional No Turn board differ in restriction from a No U-turn board?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: A No Turn sign points toward the direction you may not turn, while a No U-turn sign forbids turning around.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: On a roundabout lane-use board, what do the black dot and the dividing lines represent?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: On a roundabout lane-use sign, the dot on the left-turn arrow stands for the center of the roundabout and the lines show the separate lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: In the first two-lane roundabout example, which movements belong to the left lane versus the right lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: In the two-lane roundabout example, the left lane is only for turning left or making a U-turn, and the right lane is for going straight or turning right.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: In the three-lane roundabout example, what movements are assigned to the far-left, middle, and right lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: In the three-lane roundabout example, the far-left lane turns left or goes straight, the middle lane goes straight, and the right lane turns right.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: In the second two-lane roundabout example, how do the far-left and right lanes split movements?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: In the second two-lane roundabout lane-use sign example, the far-left lane is used only to turn left while the right lane is used to turn left or go straight.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: What side count and colors identify a Stop post, and what must your wheels do there?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: A Stop sign has eight sides and is red with white letters; come to a full stop and wait until your path is clear before going on.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: What orientation and colors identify a Yield post, and what priority rule does it enforce?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: A Yield sign is a red and white triangle pointing down with red letters, and it means you must give the right-of-way to other vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: How do Stop and Yield posts contrast in geometry, color layout, and required driver action?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: A Stop sign is red with white letters and eight sides and requires a complete stop, while a Yield sign is a downward red and white triangle that requires giving the right-of-way to other vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: What emblem sits on the back of slow rural vehicles, and how slowly might they be traveling?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: A Slow Moving Vehicle emblem is a triangle with reflective orange markings, and the vehicle carrying it may be moving at twenty-five miles per hour or less.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: What color and outline identify a No Passing Zone post, and what rule applies inside it?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: A No Passing Zone sign is a yellow pennant with black letters, and you may not pass any vehicle within that zone.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: How does the reflective orange slow-vehicle triangle differ from the yellow no-passing pennant?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: The orange Slow Moving Vehicle triangle marks a vehicle that may travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less, while the yellow No Passing Zone pennant forbids passing.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: Which two credentials legally allow a vehicle to park in a reserved accessible stall?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: A reserved parking space may be used only by a vehicle with a valid disabled parking identification permit or a valid disabled license plate.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: What colors and two outlines mark construction boards, and which three groups of workers do they protect?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: Construction signs are orange diamonds or rectangles with black letters and symbols that warn of construction, maintenance or emergency workers on or near the road.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: When black-on-orange diamond or rectangular boards appear, what three types of roadside personnel may be ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: Orange diamond or rectangular construction signs have black lettering and symbols that warn about construction, maintenance, or emergency workers on or near the road.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: What immediate speed adjustment should orange boards, cones, and markers around a work zone trigger?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Orange signs, cones and flags around a work area are your cue to slow down.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: How does Wisconsin law adjust traffic citation fines inside construction work areas?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Traffic fines are doubled in construction work areas.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: Under what sole circumstance is using a cellphone legal while driving through a Wisconsin construction zone?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: In a construction zone you may use a cellphone only to report an emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: What lies ahead of a Road Construction Flagger Ahead board, and what is your legal obligation?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: A Road Construction Flagger Ahead sign warns of a worker with a sign or flag, and you must follow that worker's directions.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: What action do Road Workers Ahead and Road Work Ahead boards share, and what extra detail does Road Work Ahead add?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Road Workers Ahead and Road Work Ahead signs both call for you to slow down or move over, and the Road Work Ahead sign says how far away the work is.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.front: How does a live flagger's command compare with the message of a Road Workers Ahead board?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.expected_back: A flagger's directions must be followed, while the Road Workers Ahead sign asks you to slow down or move over for workers ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: What shapes, colors, and six sample destination types appear on highway destination boards?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: Destination signs are square or rectangular, green or brown with white letters, and give directions and distances to places such as cities, states, airports, parks, historical sites and museums.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: What practical lane clue does the angled arrow on a highway Exit board give you?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: On an Exit sign the arrow shows which side of the road the exit is on.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: What navigation answer does a roundabout exit guide board give before you leave the circle?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: A roundabout exit sign tells you which road you will be on after leaving the roundabout at each exit.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Where do street name blades stand, and how are they mounted to show which road they label?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: Street name signs stand on almost every corner, mounted on top of a silver pole that faces the road they name.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: What kind of destinations do brown guide boards highlight, and what distance detail may they include?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: Brown destination signs point to recreational or scenic places, and some list the miles to get there.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.front: While both green and brown guide boards point to places, how do their destinations differ?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.expected_back: Green and brown guide signs both give directions to places, but the brown ones point to fun or scenic places such as parks.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: What shapes, colors, and traveler facilities define roadside service boards?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: Service signs are square or rectangular, blue with white letters or symbols, and guide you to nearby services such as camping or a hospital.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.front: How do blue roadside boards contrast in purpose with green and brown guide boards?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.expected_back: Blue signs point to services such as a hospital or camping, while green and brown signs point to destinations.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: What other name, shape, colors, and emergency purpose belong to highway mile markers?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: Mile markers, also called reference markers, are tall, thin blue or green signs with white letters that show where you are on the road and help emergency crews reach highway incidents faster.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: What three details appear on each Wisconsin mile marker, how closely are they spaced, and where do they stand?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: Each mile marker gives the travel direction, route number and mile number, and markers are spaced every one to two-tenths of a mile on the right side of the road or in the median.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.front: Since mile markers can be either blue or green, how can you tell one apart from service or destination boards?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.expected_back: Mile markers can be blue or green but are recognized by their tall, thin shape and the direction, route and mile number they carry.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: Why do numbered highway route markers use different outlines and color schemes?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: Route number signs change shape and color with the type of road and help you follow a route to your destination.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: What distinctive shape and three-color layout identify an Interstate highway marker?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: An Interstate highway sign is a shield, red on top and blue on the bottom, with white lettering.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.front: What shape, edge detail, and colors identify a Wisconsin county road marker?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.expected_back: A county road sign is a white rectangle with rounded edges and black letters.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.front: What everyday silhouette and colors identify a United States route marker compared with an interstate shield?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.expected_back: A U.S. route sign looks like a police badge and is usually grey or white with black letters, unlike the red and blue interstate shield.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.front: What iconic dairy-state shape and colors identify a Wisconsin state highway marker?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.expected_back: A state road sign is shaped like a milk jug with its spout at the bottom and is white with black letters.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.front: What three deadly mistakes must you never commit at any railroad grade crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.expected_back: Never race a train to a crossing, never stop on the tracks, and do not start across unless there is room for your vehicle on the far side.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.front: What transmission move is off-limits over rails, and when must you scan both ways?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.expected_back: Do not change gears while you are crossing railroad tracks, and look both ways before crossing even when the crossing lights are not flashing.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.front: Why do drivers routinely misjudge how much time they have before an approaching locomotive arrives?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.expected_back: Trains are big and heavy and travel faster than they appear to.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.front: What shape, colors, and symbol make up the railroad advance warning, and what does it tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.expected_back: The railroad advance warning sign is round and yellow with an X symbol and black letters, telling you a crossing is ahead and to watch for a train.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.front: What triggers flashing red lights on a crossbuck post, and when is it legal to drive across?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.expected_back: At a crossbuck with flashing lights, the lights flash when a train approaches from either direction; wait until they stop and the track is clear before going.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.front: What obligation applies where a red-and-white Yield triangle hangs beneath a white X crossbuck?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.expected_back: A white X-shaped crossbuck with a Yield sign mounted below it means you must yield to any train using the crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.front: Beyond advance warning, what extra track detail can the white X crossbuck assembly display that the yellow circle does not?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.expected_back: The round yellow railroad warning sign with an X tells you a crossing is there, while the white X-shaped crossbuck also lists how many tracks you will cross.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.front: How does a Tracks Out-of-Service plaque differ in meaning from an Exempt rail plaque?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.expected_back: A Tracks out-of-service sign means the tracks are no longer used, while an Exempt sign means only certain vehicles are excused from stopping before crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.front: What color placard stands at every highway-rail crossing with a phone number, and what two emergencies do you call in?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.expected_back: A blue Report Problem or Emergency sign with white letters stands at every highway-railroad crossing and lists a phone number for reporting a stalled vehicle on the tracks or a failed warning light.

sec05-card-sec05-F48.front: Can you rely on every multi-track railroad crossing having a number-of-tracks plaque posted?
sec05-card-sec05-F48.expected_back: Some crossings with more than one track post a number-of-tracks sign, but not all do, so always check for additional tracks before you cross.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.front: After the caboose or last car clears a double-track crossing, how long must you hold back before pulling forward?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.expected_back: When a crossing has two sets of tracks, wait until the train is far enough away that you can see the other tracks are clear.

sec05-card-sec05-F49.front: What two maneuvers around a railroad crossing gate are strictly prohibited?
sec05-card-sec05-F49.expected_back: A railroad gate comes down when a train approaches; never drive around it or under it while it is moving up or down.

sec05-card-sec05-F50.front: At a railroad crossing equipped with an audible bell or horn alongside lights, when may you start across?
sec05-card-sec05-F50.expected_back: Where a crossing has a bell or horn with its lights, do not cross until the sound has stopped.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Which three items must you carry whenever you drive, and what vehicle condition should you verify first?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Leaving home without valid paperwork or a roadworthy car turns a routine traffic stop into avoidable citations.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Before putting the car in motion, what belt and visibility steps must you finish inside the cabin?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Fixing mirrors or buckling passengers while rolling pulls your eyes and hands away during critical first seconds.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: What does right-of-way determine where paths meet, and what assumption about vehicles on the right is dangerous?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Treating right-of-way as an automatic pass for whoever sits on the right ignores signals, arrival order, and safety.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Regardless of technical priority rules, when does Wisconsin law always require you to yield?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Having the legal turn never excuses hitting a walker, cyclist, or driver when yielding prevents impact.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Which road users already inside an intersection keep priority over waiting traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Launching on a fresh green before walkers, cyclists, or turning cars finish clearing causes intersection broadsides.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Who proceeds first at a four-way stop, and how is a simultaneous arrival broken?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Drivers and cyclists clear four-way stops smoothly when everyone tracks stop-line order and yields right on ties.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: At a four-way stop, does sitting to another driver's right let you go ahead if they stopped earlier?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Test questions bait drivers into picking the right-hand car even when another vehicle clearly stopped first.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: When you reach an open intersection with zero signs or signals, which direction gets priority?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Unmarked neighborhood corners rely on yielding to traffic approaching from your right so two cars never collide.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Whom must you yield to when entering a roundabout or reaching an uncontrolled T-intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Drivers already inside a roundabout circle or traveling straight across the top of a T hold continuous flow.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Contrast who gets the right-of-way at an uncontrolled four-way corner versus an uncontrolled T-intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: On the terminating stem of an unmarked T, you yield to through traffic from both left and right.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: As you approach a roundabout entrance, which stream of vehicles holds the right-of-way?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Forcing circulating drivers to brake inside the circle jams the whole roundabout and triggers side-swipe crashes.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: How far back must you stop for a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, and how long do you wait?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Stopping at least ten feet back keeps engine noise from confusing a blind pedestrian until they leave the pavement.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: Does a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog lose priority when crossing away from an intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Unlike standard mid-block rules, blind pedestrians keep absolute priority anywhere on the road with a ten-foot buffer.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which vehicles keep priority when someone passes you, when you turn left or U-turn, or when sirens sound?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Speeding up on a passer, cutting across oncoming lanes, or blocking flashing emergency units creates high-speed collisions.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: Before turning left or swinging a U-turn, or while being overtaken on either side, whom do you let go?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Checking both oncoming traffic ahead and overtaking lanes beside you prevents mid-turn T-bones and sideswipes.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What core safety goal should govern your speed choice, and what named Wisconsin rule gauges your following gap?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Keeping enough time cushion to stop cleanly prevents chain-reaction rear-enders when lead traffic slams the brakes.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: How do you use a roadside landmark to measure a four-second following gap, and what proves you are too close?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Passing that tree or sign before finishing one-thousand-four proves your speed outruns a safe reaction cushion.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: How do you adjust your four-second following count when rain, snow, ice, or heavy traffic show up?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Wet or icy pavement stretches braking distance while heavy traffic multiplies sudden slowdowns ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: What is Wisconsin's baseline following time gap, and how much time does each poor condition tack onto it?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Stacking one extra second per hazard turns rain plus heavy traffic into at least a six-second buffer.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What does a posted speed limit represent legally, and may you push above it to pass a slower car?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Many drivers wrongly think passing grants a temporary speed-limit bonus, which earns speeding tickets in Wisconsin.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Is a driver ever allowed to exceed the posted speed limit briefly to finish passing another vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: If getting around a vehicle ahead would push your speedometer past the posted number, stay behind instead.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: How does Wisconsin law treat racing and reckless driving, and what roadside check keeps your speed legal?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Speed zones drop fast entering towns, so steady sign scanning stops unintentional speeding citations.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: When no speed sign is posted in a Wisconsin residential neighborhood, what limit applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Driveways, parked cars, and neighborhood foot traffic demand a twenty-five-mile-per-hour cap whenever signs are absent.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: What is the standard Wisconsin school-zone speed limit when children are present?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Dropping down to fifteen miles per hour around kids gives you stopping margin if someone darts off the curb.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: In unposted outlying sections of Wisconsin cities and villages, what maximum speed limit applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Less-built-up city fringes allow thirty-five miles per hour until residential blocks or lower signs appear.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Compare Wisconsin's default speed limits across active school zones, residential blocks, and unposted outlying town edges?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Stepping cleanly by tens from fifteen to twenty-five to thirty-five locks in all three local statutory limits.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Why might driving right at the posted speed limit still be unsafe on a foggy or slick day?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Speed signs set the ceiling for clear dry pavement, so poor visibility or slick surfaces demand easing off.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: Why can creeping far below traffic speed trigger crashes and earn a police ticket just like speeding?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Bottlenecking normal flow frustrates trailing drivers into risky passes and sudden rear-end braking.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Which lane belongs to you when traveling slower than surrounding traffic on a multi-lane road?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Camping slowly in left or center lanes blocks overtaking flow and forces dangerous right-side passes.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How do you avoid impeding-traffic tickets and crashes when others move faster on a multi-lane road?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Moving with legal traffic speed or tucking into the far-right lane keeps overtaking lanes clear and predictable.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: What speed should you target in flowing traffic and while merging onto a highway?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Merging way slower than highway traffic forces fast-moving vehicles behind you to slam brakes or swerve.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: How should you use a highway on-ramp's acceleration lane, and whose duty is finding a safe merging gap?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Counting on freeway drivers to move over instead of spotting your own gap causes ramp-end sideswipes.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: Even if through drivers sometimes courtesy-shift left, who bears legal responsibility for merging safely from an on-ramp?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Through highway traffic holds lane priority, meaning the entering driver must time speed and space cleanly.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: Where should your gradual braking happen when exiting a highway?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes early in the live highway lane surprises high-speed traffic right behind your bumper.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Pair the highway acceleration lane and deceleration lane with their ramps and speed changes?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Keeping speed changes tucked onto the ramps protects main highway lanes from sudden slowdowns or crawls.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What happens to the space needed for turning, slowing, or stopping as your speed climbs?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Momentum grows rapidly with speed, so trimming pace early when roads tighten keeps turns and stops controlled.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: How many seconds down the road ahead should you scan to maintain solid vehicle control?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Aiming eyes ten to fifteen seconds up the road spots brake lights and lane closures long before panic stops.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: Does Wisconsin's ten-to-fifteen-second rule measure following distance or visual look-ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Exam writers love swapping the four-second following count with the ten-to-fifteen-second eye-lead horizon.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: Which road shapes, busy places, and fresh weather call for slowing down, and what is best on icy roads?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Blind crests, fresh slick precipitation, and bustling school or shopping zones slash grip and sightlines at once.
sec03-card-sec03-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Slow for curves, crowds; skip ice

visual_sync.text_span: Slow for curves, crowds; skip ice

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Beyond standard street corners, which everyday crossings count as intersections under Wisconsin rules?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Recognizing driveways, mall entrances, and train tracks as true intersections keeps your conflict scan sharp everywhere.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: What three things must you verify before rolling into any intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Confirming an open exit lane ahead keeps your car from getting stranded mid-intersection when signals change.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: How should you handle an intersection when obstructions block your cross-street view?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Creeping forward with your foot hovering ready over the brake lets you spot cross traffic before your hood intrudes.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: Which three common roadside objects hide approaching cross traffic near intersections, and how should you approach?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Approaching blind corners slowly buys precious reaction feet if a hidden car or cyclist pops out.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: Even with a green light, why must your intersection check sweep left, then right, then left once more?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Looking left a second time catches distracted red-light runners in the first lane your bumper enters.
sec03-card-sec03-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Left, right, left; others blow signs

visual_sync.text_span: Left, right, left; others blow signs

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: What two crash risks come from slamming the brakes late instead of spotting slowdowns early?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Easing onto the brakes early flashes brake lights in time for trailing drivers while keeping tires planted.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: Why must you keep your transmission in gear rather than coasting in neutral while moving?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: Rolling disconnected in neutral strips engine braking and instant throttle response if a hazard demands swerving.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.question_text: What driving habit is called coasting, and why does Wisconsin's handbook tell you to avoid it?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.teaching_text: Knowing coasting specifically means shifting into neutral while rolling makes this classic safety question effortless.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.question_text: When curves, hills, darkness, or fog cut your forward view under ten to fifteen seconds, what is required?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.teaching_text: Outrunning your ten-to-fifteen-second sight window guarantees you cannot stop short of a stalled car in the gloom.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.question_text: Which four directions around your vehicle should regular driving and mirror checks cover?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.teaching_text: Cycling eyes across side mirrors, windshield, and rearview mirror keeps a live 360-degree mental map.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.question_text: What four checks protect you before driving across railroad tracks?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.teaching_text: Never trusting quiet tracks, and verifying full car space beyond the rails, prevents getting trapped in a train's path.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.question_text: Besides looking and listening for an approaching train, what space check is mandatory before entering railroad tracks?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.teaching_text: Pulling onto tracks behind backed-up traffic can pin your bumper across the rails when crossing gates drop.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.question_text: Why should you keep eyes moving forward instead of staring at traffic stops or roadside scenes?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.teaching_text: Drivers ahead often brake unexpectedly near flashing squad lights while rubberneckers drift or plow into them.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.question_text: How should you manage space around large trucks and cars lingering right beside your doors?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.teaching_text: Staying out of side-by-side clusters and giving rigs wide sightlines preserves an escape lane if someone swerves.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.question_text: Which standard time-gap rule sets your forward buffer whenever following another vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.teaching_text: Anchoring your forward cushion at four seconds gives brakes and reflexes room to work at any speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F41.question_text: Which road surfaces, passing situations, and lead vehicles require stretching your gap past four seconds?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.teaching_text: Large rigs block your view while motorcycles and bikes stop fast or wobble on slick pavement.

sec03-card-sec03-F42.question_text: Which five load, rear-traffic, emergency, rail, or grade situations call for more than four seconds ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.teaching_text: Extra forward buffer absorbs trailer weight, hill rollback, rail stops, and gentle braking when someone rides your bumper.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.question_text: Along with following motorcycles or bicycles, which two stopping or crossing spots require extra room ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.teaching_text: Vehicles ahead may roll back slightly starting on an upgrade or stop abruptly before railroad tracks.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.question_text: How often should you glance at your rearview mirror, and what is the safe response to a tailgater?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.teaching_text: Brake-checking invites a collision, whereas easing off the gas gradually encourages an impatient tailgater to pass.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.question_text: Contrast Wisconsin's six-to-eight-second rhythm against its four-second rule so you never mix them up?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.teaching_text: Keeping six-to-eight seconds tied to rearview checks prevents confusing it with your four-second front gap.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.question_text: According to Wisconsin's handbook, how do you safely encourage a close tailgater to go around you?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.teaching_text: Gradually shedding speed lowers crash energy and opens passing opportunities without startling the bumper-rider behind you.

sec03-card-sec03-F44.question_text: Which two habits help drivers behind you anticipate your moves, and whose blind rear needs extra room?
sec03-card-sec03-F44.teaching_text: Predictable speed and early turn signals prevent panic stops behind you, especially near box vans lacking rear windows.

sec03-card-sec03-F45.question_text: Where must passenger pick-ups happen, and how should a slower driver handle multi-lane traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F45.teaching_text: Stopping in live travel lanes for curb drop-offs or hogging left lanes creates sudden rear-end hazards.

sec03-card-sec03-F46.question_text: Before driving across opposing traffic or a multi-lane roadway, what three checks keep you from getting stranded?
sec03-card-sec03-F46.teaching_text: Waiting until your whole car can clear every lane prevents blocking fast cross traffic mid-roadway.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: What five checks and actions must you complete before starting any turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Skipping a shoulder blind-spot glance before turning clips cyclists or cars tucked right beside your rear fender.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: Why are last-second changes of plan unsafe, and what must you check before turning into a driveway?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Slamming brakes for a surprise side road gives tailing drivers zero reaction room to avoid rear-ending your bumper.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: What two lane errors must you avoid mid-turn, and why do trucks and buses need extra space?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Long wheelbases force buses and semis across the center stripe on tight corners, crushing cars crowded up to the line.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: If a turning bus swings across the center stripe, may your car cross it too, or what should you do?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Copying a wide bus swing in a passenger car cuts straight into oncoming lanes and earns an automatic road-test fail.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: How should you position your car, scan for walkers, and wait inside an intersection for a left turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Pulling halfway forward near the center line keeps sightlines open around opposing left turners while checking the far crosswalk.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Which way must your front wheels point while waiting to turn left, and what happens if rear-ended otherwise?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Pre-turning your tires left turns any minor rear bumper tap into a deadly head-on shove into oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: How does a U-turn reverse your travel direction, and how risky is it even where legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Swinging across multiple lanes exposes the broadside of your car to fast oncoming and cross-street traffic simultaneously.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What three things must you verify before starting any U-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Overlooking a corner turn restriction or fast-closing traffic turns a quick turnaround into a broadside wreck or ticket.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: Under what condition is a U-turn legal on any rural two-lane highway?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Blind hills and curves on country roads hide fast vehicles, so clear sightlines matter even where rural turnarounds are permitted.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: What motion defines a proper U-turn, and what can override its rural two-lane permission?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Stopping mid-road to reverse turns a legal continuous sweep into a hazardous three-point block on fast country pavement.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: When two or more lanes turn together at an intersection, which lane must you finish in?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Drifting wide from the inside turn bay into the middle or outer lane sideswipes the car turning right beside you.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: Which lane must you occupy before making a right turn off a four-lane road?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Turning right from an inside lane cuts directly across the bow of traffic cruising straight along the right curb.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: On what kind of street belongs a Y-turn, and what official test requires you to demonstrate one?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Practicing crisp signals and shoulder glances on quiet side streets preps you for a guaranteed road-test grading item.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How does a Y-turn differ in motion, setting, and exam testing from a U-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Attempting a stop-and-reverse turnaround on a busy arterial instead of a quiet neighborhood street risks a double-direction collision.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: What exact sequence of signaling, checking, positioning, and stopping makes up step one of a Y-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Pulling tight against the right edge first gives your front bumper maximum turning radius to clear the opposite curb.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: What four actions take you across the street in step two of a Y-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Forgetting the left blinker or shoulder check before swinging across the street fails the road-test observation checklist.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: How do you execute step three's reverse and step four's pull-away to finish a Y-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Backing only far enough to clear the curb keeps your rear bumper off lawns and driveways while you scan both ways.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: Which numbered step of the Y-turn is the sole reversing move, and where must you look first?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Examiners watch your head turn over your right shoulder during step three instead of staring down at a dashboard screen.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: Under what two narrow conditions may you drive onto a paved shoulder to pass another vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Passing moving traffic on a shoulder kicks up debris and surprises cars pulling right into driveways or breakdowns.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: Which lane handles passing on multi-lane highways, and why is overtaking on the right dangerous?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Right-side blind spots stretch wider than left-side ones, making drivers drift back right without spotting you.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How does standard highway overtaking contrast with passing along a paved shoulder?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Permit questions test whether you treat paved shoulders like bonus right-hand passing lanes behind slow cruise traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: What two courteous, safety-first actions should you take whenever another vehicle tries to pass you?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Speeding up races the passer against oncoming traffic and traps both cars in a high-speed head-on pinch.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: What four-part routine must you follow every single time you change lanes?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Sweeping across two or three lanes in one diagonal cut hides cars merging into the same middle space.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: What do we call the zones checked over your left and right shoulders, and why can mirrors not cover them?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Whole motorcycles and compact sedans fit inside rear-quarter zones even when side mirrors are aimed well.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Why does glancing at rearview and side mirrors alone fall short right before switching lanes?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Relying strictly on glass without turning your chin toward the target lane is one of the top road-test deductions.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: How many vehicles may you overtake in one pass, on which side, and why?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Stringing multiple cars into one two-lane pass eats up clear road fast when an oncoming car crests a hill.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: May you hang out in the passing lane or push above the posted speed limit to finish overtaking?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Many new drivers falsely believe state law grants a ten-mile-per-hour burst cushion over the speed limit while passing.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: What space must exist ahead of the car you pass before pulling out, and must other drivers make room?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Pulling alongside a tight convoy with nowhere to tuck back in leaves you stranded nose-to-nose with oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: How does Wisconsin law treat the speed limit and the passed driver's lane duty while you overtake?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Expecting slower cars to edge onto the shoulder or assuming speed limits flex during passes fails classic permit questions.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: What exact sight in your inside rearview mirror confirms you have cleared a passed vehicle enough to merge right?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Cutting back right before spotting both lamps clips their front fender or forces them to slam the brakes.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: After overtaking on the left, how do you verify clean buffer space before pulling back into the travel lane?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Side mirrors distort distance, whereas catching the entire front grille in your center mirror guarantees clean clearance.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: Because rear visibility is tight, how far and how fast should you ever drive in reverse?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Creeping at walking speed gives toddlers, pets, or shopping carts time to clear and lets you stop on a dime.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: Instead of trusting mirrors and cameras alone while backing, how should you position your body and get help?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Wide camera lenses miss side cross-traffic and overhang corners that turning your shoulders or using a spotter catches.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: What scan comes right after backing, and how must you handle missing a highway exit or street turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: Backing up on a highway shoulder or ramp puts reverse lights directly against seventy-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: If you sail right past your highway exit ramp, what is the sole safe recovery move?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Every year fatal pileups happen when panicked drivers brake and reverse along exit gore stripes.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: Whose responsibility is keeping a parked car hazard-free, and where does that normally place your car?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Leaving a rear corner sticking into an active lane invites distracted or night drivers to clip your parked car.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: Which three curb markings, fixtures, or posts forbid parking your vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Blocking hydrants or yellow loading zones delays fire hoses in emergencies and earns immediate tows or tickets.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: At what speed should you pull into a spot, and how do you secure automatic or manual cars on flat ground?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Engaging both transmission lock and the parking brake keeps your car anchored even if a bumper tap nudges the pawl.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: Which direction must you turn your front wheels before shifting into park when facing uphill beside a curb?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Aiming tires away from the curb lets the back of the right front tire catch cleanly against concrete if brakes slip.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking uphill along a road with no curb?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Without a concrete curb to catch a left-turned tire, turning right makes a runaway car roll off the shoulder instead of across traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: Which way do your front wheels turn when parked downhill, and what brake rule applies on every slope?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Gravity pulls a downhill car forward, so turning right aims the front tires into the curb or off the road shoulder.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: Out of all hill-parking setups, which sole setup turns wheels left while every other case turns right?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Memorizing that uphill-with-curb is the lone left-turn outlier solves every hill-parking question in two seconds.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.question_text: What hazards must you scan for before parallel parking, and how much longer than your car should the gap measure?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.teaching_text: Squeezing into a tight gap shorter than three extra feet traps bumpers and leaves zero swing angle toward the curb.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.question_text: How do you signal and position your car alongside the front parked vehicle to start parallel parking?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.teaching_text: Stopping closer than two feet risks scraping side mirrors as your front end swings outward during the initial turn.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: In parallel parking, how does your side-by-side starting gap compare with the extra length needed in the curb space?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Keeping two feet side-clearance separate from three-to-six feet length-clearance stops test-takers from swapping the two numbers.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.question_text: Once stopped parallel to the lead car, which way do you crank the wheel and how do you start moving?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.teaching_text: Turning sharply toward your target curb—right on two-way streets or left on one-way left curbs—sets the forty-five-degree entry line.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.question_text: What alignment landmark tells you to straighten the steering wheel and glide straight back into the space?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.teaching_text: Holding full lock too long drives your rear tire hard over the curb before the nose clears the car ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.question_text: What clearance landmark cues you to crank the steering wheel sharply the opposite way while backing in?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.teaching_text: Cranking away too early clips your front corner against the parked car's rear taillight.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.question_text: How do you finish positioning your wheels, curb gap, and front-and-rear bumper cushions in a parallel spot?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.teaching_text: Parking within twelve inches keeps doors out of bike and car traffic while two-foot buffers let boxed neighbors pull out.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.question_text: At the end of a clean parallel park, how does your target distance from the curb differ from your distance to other cars?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.teaching_text: Road-test examiners check curb tightness and front-and-rear bumper spacing right before asking you to pull back out.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.question_text: What four lighting or braking tools plus space habit broadcast your position and plans to surrounding drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.teaching_text: Predictable lighting and generous cushions prevent surprises when traffic slows suddenly on busy corridors.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.question_text: Why should you stay out of the driver's seat when feeling intensely worried, excited, afraid, angry, or down?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.teaching_text: Heavy emotions tunnel your attention away from mirrors and tempt aggressive speed or risky gap choices.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.question_text: What safety purpose does the horn serve, and when do you use a light tap versus a hard press?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.teaching_text: Laying on a long blast in mild situations startles drivers into swerving, whereas a firm blast saves lives in true emergencies.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.question_text: How do you match horn pressure to polite awareness versus an imminent crash?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.teaching_text: Using the horn as an anger vent instead of a crash-prevention alert escalates road rage without making anyone safer.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.question_text: Even if your car features automatic daytime sensors, what manual headlight habit must you still know?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.teaching_text: Daytime fog and snow stay bright enough to fool auto sensors, leaving your rear taillights completely dark to fast traffic behind.

sec04-card-sec04-F43.question_text: What sight distance limit and exact sunset-to-sunrise window make low-beam headlights legally mandatory?
sec04-card-sec04-F43.teaching_text: Driving on daytime running lights past thirty minutes after sunset leaves taillights off and draws an instant equipment stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F44.question_text: Under what wiper and weather conditions does the manual recommend switching on your low beams?
sec04-card-sec04-F44.teaching_text: Low beams cut glare bounce off wet droplets while lighting your taillights through highway spray.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.question_text: How does Wisconsin separate legally required low-beam situations from recommended low-beam situations?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.teaching_text: Exam questions specifically test whether wiper-on headlights are a statutory mandate or a strongly recommended habit in Wisconsin.

sec04-card-sec04-F45.question_text: How much farther do high beams reach than low beams, where do they help, and when must you dim them?
sec04-card-sec04-F45.teaching_text: Blinding an approaching driver with high beams can send their car drifting straight across the center line into yours.

sec04-card-sec04-F46.question_text: Where should your eyes look against blinding oncoming brights, and when is the sole time to use parking lights?
sec04-card-sec04-F46.teaching_text: Tracking the white right edge stripe keeps you centered without frying night vision, and cruising on dim parking lights is unsafe.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.question_text: How do high beams and parking lights stand at opposite ends of driving versus stationary use?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.teaching_text: Driving at dusk on parking lights makes your vehicle seem much farther away than it really is to turning traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F47.question_text: What sequence comes before moving, and how early in time and distance do you signal an intersection turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F47.teaching_text: Flicking the stalk mid-turn warns nobody; signaling three seconds ahead lets following drivers ease off smoothly.

sec04-card-sec04-F48.question_text: When your target driveway sits right beyond an intersection, at what moment should you flick on your blinker?
sec04-card-sec04-F48.teaching_text: Signaling before the cross street tricks waiting side-street cars into pulling out directly across your bow.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.question_text: How does blinker timing shift between turning at the cross street versus turning into a lot just beyond it?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.teaching_text: Holding your blinker until clearing the cross street stops right-turning drivers ahead from misreading your intent.

sec04-card-sec04-F49.question_text: When may hand gestures stand in for blinkers, and what left-arm position marks left, right, and slow or stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F49.teaching_text: Burned-out bulbs, bright sun glare, or towed trailers can hide taillights, making crisp left-arm signals essential.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.question_text: How do the three driver-side arm angles map to left turn, right turn, and braking?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.teaching_text: Cyclists and vintage vehicles use these exact three left-arm angles daily, so you must recognize them instantly.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Where do traffic signals typically stand, and how are red, yellow, and green stacked from top to bottom?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Standard vertical stacking lets color-blind drivers and glare-struck eyes read active phases by lens position alone.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Instead of a full three-lens housing, what simpler setup hangs over many rural country intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Rural crossroads often pair flashing yellow on the main highway with flashing red on the smaller side road.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: How must you treat an intersection whenever its traffic signal loses power or malfunctions?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Breezing through a dead signal without halting sets up high-speed T-bone wrecks when cross traffic assumes the same.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: When a traffic light goes dark or glitches out, which control rule applies instead of a yield or green?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Permit distractors tempt drivers to treat main-road outages like yields, which fails the Wisconsin knowledge exam.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Whose command wins when a uniformed police officer directs traffic underneath a working signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Officers managing crashes, parades, or stadium surges wave cars past red bulbs deliberately to clear bottlenecks safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What two conditions must happen after your complete stop at a steady red light before going straight?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Jumping forward on fresh green before cross-street stragglers finish clearing invites an intersection collision.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: What two-step sequence applies when you roll up to a flashing red traffic light?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Waiting endlessly for green at a midnight flasher backs up traffic, whereas rolling without stopping runs the red.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: After halting your wheels completely, how does a steady red light differ from a flashing red light?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Both lights demand a dead wheel stop first; only what happens next separates waiting out the cycle from proceeding clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: What must you do when facing a steady red turn arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Unlike a standard circular red ball, a steady red arrow locks down that turn completely until the arrow phase changes.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: How do you handle a turn lane controlled by a flashing red arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Halting fully before checking oncoming gaps keeps turning drivers from rolling into fast cross traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: What separates your post-stop move at a steady red arrow from your move at a flashing red arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Turning after stopping on a steady red arrow earns a red-light ticket, whereas waiting on flashing red stalls the bay.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What two conditions make turning right on a steady red light legal in Wisconsin?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Always scan corners and overhead mast arms for No Turn on Red boards before edging forward after stopping.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What exact street-to-street combination is required to make a legal left turn on red?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Only two intersecting one-way streets let you hug the left curb around the corner without crossing opposing lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How do street-type restrictions differ between turning right on red and turning left on red?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Test questions frequently dangle left-on-red from a two-way street onto a one-way street—which is illegal in Wisconsin.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: How must every legal turn on red start, handle conflicting road users, and finish?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Swinging wide across multiple lanes during a turn on red clips cross-street cars cruising legally on green.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What phase comes right after steady yellow, and what must you do if you have not entered yet?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Yellow clears the intersection rather than inviting approaches from back up the block to mash the gas.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: What should you do if the signal switches to yellow after your car is already inside the intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Panic-stopping or backing up mid-intersection strands your car directly across cross-street lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: What three-step habit applies when approaching a flashing yellow signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Side-street drivers facing stop posts or red flashers sometimes misjudge your speed at rural junctions.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Before you reach the crosswalk, how does steady yellow differ from flashing yellow?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Stopping dead for a flashing yellow surprises tailing traffic, whereas coasting into a steady yellow runs the impending red.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: What transition does a steady yellow arrow announce, and how should you respond?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Pushing late into a dying arrow phase leaves you turning across oncoming lanes right as their green launches.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How do you safely complete a turn under a flashing yellow arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Flashing yellow arrows mean oncoming traffic holds a green light, so every gap judgment rests on you.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: How does the meaning of a steady yellow arrow contrast with a flashing yellow arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Modern four-section turn heads use both arrows—flashing while permissive turns run, then steady right before locking red.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: Even when cruising straight on a steady green light, whom must you still yield to?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Ambulances, fire trucks, and walkers legally in the crosswalk hold priority even when your overhead bulb shines green.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: When you sit first in line and your red light flips green, what must happen before you pull out?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Two-second left-right scans before touching the gas save front-row drivers from red-light runners every single day.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Why may you turn left on a steady circular green light only when a clean gap opens?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Turning left in front of approaching through-cars is the single most common right-of-way crash at signalized corners.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: What traffic protection comes with a steady green arrow, and whom must you still watch out for?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Conflicting vehicle phases are held red, yet late joggers or confused pedestrians can still step off the corner.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: How does turning left on a steady green ball contrast with turning left under a steady green arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Assuming protected arrow priority when only a circular green shines pulls you straight across live oncoming lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Why does neither a green arrow nor a steady green ball ever grant blind, unconditional right-of-way?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Green grants permission to proceed only after verifying pedestrians and emergency responders are clear of your path.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: What four things do pavement lines, symbols, and stripe colors tell you about the road beneath your tires?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Reading stripe color instantly tells you whether adjacent lanes run with you or carry head-on opposing cars.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Which color stripe marks your right travel edge, and which color marks the left edge of lanes going your way?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: If yellow ever sits along your right window, you are facing the wrong way on a ramp or divided highway.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: How do white interior stripes and the left-side yellow stripe divide duties along your travel lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Keeping white between parallel lanes and yellow along the leftmost edge orients drivers cleanly in fog or snow.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: What does a dashed white stripe allow, and what rule does a white pavement arrow set for its lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Ignoring a painted turn arrow and shooting straight through an intersection cuts off neighboring turn traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: Under Wisconsin rules, what are the sole two reasons you may cross a solid white line between lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Routine weaving across solid white stripes near intersections or ramps draws a lane-violation stop.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: How does Wisconsin's rule for crossing dashed white paint differ from crossing solid white paint between lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Exam questions specifically test the hazard and next-block-turn exceptions on solid white lane dividers.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Where exact spot must your front tires stop near a crosswalk, and where must you never rest?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Parking your hood across pedestrian stripes forces parents with strollers and wheelchair users out into moving traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Besides street corners, where else can crosswalks sit, and what extra control might walkers have there?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Campus, trail, and downtown mid-block crossings catch drivers who only scan for walkers at four-way intersections.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: What traffic directions do solid yellow stripes divide, and what general passing rule do two solid yellows set?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Hills, curves, and heavy access points hide oncoming cars wherever double yellow lines run down the middle.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: When may you turn across a double solid yellow center line?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Wait for a clean oncoming gap with wheels straight before turning left across twin yellow stripes into a lot.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: What slow-vehicle exception allows passing across double yellow in Wisconsin, and which vehicle is excluded?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Wide tractors and combines often turn left into unmarked field entrances without turn blinkers, making double-yellow passes deadly.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: What are Wisconsin's two legal reasons to cross double solid yellow, plus the farm-machinery rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: That farm-equipment carve-out is a signature Wisconsin permit-test question that trips up guessers.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: What maneuver does a single dashed yellow center line allow, and what caution stays in force?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Dashed yellow never promises an empty lane; oncoming cars can still crest a rise or pull out from driveways.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: How does standard passing permission contrast between a single dashed yellow line and double solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Reading solid versus broken yellow instantly tells you whether road geometry provides safe passing sight distance.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: Where one dashed yellow stripe runs alongside one solid yellow stripe, who holds permission to pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Crossing when the solid bar touches your lane pulls you into oncoming blind spots before sightlines open.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: Along mixed solid-and-dashed yellow center stripes, how do you know instantly whether passing applies to you?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Ignoring the far stripe and reading only your adjacent stripe prevents backwards guesses under exam pressure.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: Besides yellow center paint, what else may mark where passing zones start and end?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Snow-covered rural highways hide yellow paint in winter, making roadside passing and no-passing pennants vital.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: Which two maneuvers belong in a shared center lane, who may enter it, and what arrows mark it?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Using a center left-turn bay as a merge-acceleration runway or passing chute risks a head-on collision.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: When and why may you cross the outer solid yellow border into a shared center lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Scan ahead inside the center bay before pulling in so an opposing driver is not claiming the exact same spot.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: How do reversible lanes schedule flow, and what pavement stripes and overhead hardware control them?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Checking live overhead gantries every trip keeps commuters out of lanes switched over to opposing rush-hour flow.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: How do shared center turn lanes and reversible lanes differ in both yellow edge stripes and purpose?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Mixing up twin-dashed reversible lanes with solid-and-dashed turn bays is a classic diagram question on permit tests.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: Above a reversible lane, what does a red X, a green arrow, and a yellow X each command?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Yellow X warns the lane direction is flipping, so merge cleanly toward a green-arrow lane right away.
sec06-card-sec06-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Red closed, green open, yellow vacate

visual_sync.text_span: Red closed, green open, yellow vacate

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: Who may travel in a reserved lane, what symbol often marks it, and may other cars cruise there?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Cruising down a diamond-marked bus, bike, or carpool lane in an unauthorized car draws an immediate lane citation.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: How close to your corner may you enter a reserved lane to turn, and how do you handle cyclists there?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Cutting across in front of a moving cyclist causes a classic right-hook crash; merge behind them instead.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: What exact distance cap limits how early general traffic can enter a reserved lane for a turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Entering blocks early turns a corner turn allowance into illegal cruising inside a bus or bike lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: What time details are often posted on bus and carpool lane boards?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Checking posted rush-hour windows tells you whether a curb lane is restricted right now or open to general traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: Which three surface paint colors may highlight bus and bike lanes, and what guides your move?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Bright red bus corridors and green bike conflict zones stand out visually so turning drivers spot dedicated lanes immediately.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: What is a highway flex lane, what stripe borders it, and what triggers its opening?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: Never drive left of that solid yellow shoulder line unless active overhead signs and green arrows open the flex lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.question_text: Which class of vehicles is strictly prohibited from driving in a Wisconsin flex lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.teaching_text: Narrow shoulder clearances and median barriers leave insufficient width and stopping room for heavy commercial rigs.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: Even when a green overhead arrow opens a highway flex lane, may large trucks pull into it?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: Test questions check whether you know the heavy-truck ban overrides an active green flex-lane arrow.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.question_text: If a crash or stalled car blocks a flex lane ahead, how do overhead beacons redirect traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.teaching_text: Because flex lanes occupy the emergency shoulder, overhead X beacons clear the strip fast for responders and stalled cars.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.question_text: Above a Wisconsin flex lane, what do the green arrow, yellow X, and red X each mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.teaching_text: Merging back into general-purpose lanes promptly on yellow X prevents running up onto a stalled car under red X.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: Over a flex lane, how does a yellow X differ in urgency and meaning from a red X?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Yellow X gives you transition space to blend into general lanes before the flex shoulder locks down completely.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.question_text: Which roadside panel marks the downstream end of a flex lane, and where do you move?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.teaching_text: Blending back into general-purpose lanes smoothly at the Merge panel prevents driving onto an unopened shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What two prep steps belong before every trip, and what is the smartest call when roads look icy or unsafe?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: No driving skill beats skipping an unnecessary trip when freezing rain or glare ice turns highways treacherous.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: What does the handbook call heavily worn tires, and how do they hurt bad-weather safety?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Smooth worn-down tread cannot bite wet or snowy asphalt, sliding much farther every time you press the brake.
sec08-card-sec08-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Bald tires cut grip, stretch stops

visual_sync.text_span: Bald tires cut grip, stretch stops

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Which two distinct mechanical drawbacks make bald tires dangerous?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Worn tread hurts you twice—your car breaks loose easier in turns and needs extra car lengths to halt.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: How does reduced visibility trick your eyes when judging the speed of other vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Fog and heavy rain wash out visual contrast, tricking drivers into pulling out ahead of fast-closing traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Why shouldn't you trust that a slow-looking car in fog or heavy rain is taking its time?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Low-contrast haze masks true closing speed, meaning that dim silhouette could reach your bumper far sooner than expected.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Which two things become harder to judge about oncoming traffic after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Two floating points of headlight in pitch darkness offer few depth cues until the approaching car is close.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What three adjustments should you make whenever fog, rain, or haze cuts visibility?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Dropping pace, covering the brake mentally, and lighting your headlamps buys time when obstacles emerge late out of mist.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: What is the best decision when roads are snow-packed, icy, slippery, or flooded by downpours?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Waiting out flooded lanes or ice storms at home avoids hydroplaning, spinouts, and stranded-vehicle rescues altogether.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: During cold severe weather, which parts of a highway freeze over before regular roadbed?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Elevated concrete loses heat from both top and bottom in winter wind while soil insulates standard pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: On cold, damp days, which three spots along a route are prime hiding places for ice?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Tree-shaded curves and elevated spans stay below freezing long after winter sun dries open straightaways.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Why can your tires suddenly break loose on a bridge or shady bend when the open highway felt dry?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Clear grip on sunny pavement lulls drivers into keeping highway speed right onto a frozen overpass deck.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: Besides snow and bridges, which three everyday conditions make pavement surprisingly slippery?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Thirty-two-degree wet ice, oil floated by fresh raindrops, and deep shoulder puddles all slash tire grip instantly.
sec08-card-sec08-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Near freezing, first rain, shoulder water

visual_sync.text_span: Near freezing, first rain, shoulder water

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Why are the opening minutes of a rain shower dangerous rather than mild?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Initial drops mix with accumulated tire rubber and oil drips before heavier rain washes the film away.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: When you have no choice and must drive on slick pavement, how should you handle speed, brakes, and steering?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Gentle inputs preserve whatever limited tire friction remains, whereas stabbing pedals or jerking the wheel snaps traction.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: In a vehicle without anti-lock brakes, how do you slow down on slippery pavement without locking the wheels?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Light squeeze-and-release pulses let standard wheels keep turning so your front tires still steer.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: How does universal slick-road braking advice connect with the specific technique for cars without ABS?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Every driver avoids abrupt pedal stabs on ice, and non-ABS drivers add gentle pumping to prevent lockup.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: What happens during hydroplaning, and how do bald tires change the speed where it starts?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Without tread grooves to channel water out, worn-out tires float onto a water wedge even at city speeds.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Which three exact moves bring your car safely through hydroplaning?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Turning or braking while floating cocks the front wheels sideways so the car spins violently once rubber touches asphalt.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Why must you resist both braking and steering while your tires are hydroplaning?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Water offers zero directional bite—only easing off the gas straight ahead lets tires sink cleanly back onto pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: How does the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook describe what your tires are doing during a skid?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Once sideways slip overwhelms grip, tires skip and chatter across pavement until smooth steering aligns them with travel.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: When a skid starts, what do you do with your brake foot and your steering wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Hitting the brake locks sliding tires worse, whereas steering toward your intended lane points the front wheels home.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What steering adjustment must you make right as a skidding car begins to straighten out?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Holding recovery lock too long whips the tail into an opposite pendulum fishtail across the other side.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: What three-part sequence recovers a skidding vehicle cleanly back into its lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Staying off brakes, aiming down-lane, and unwinding the wheel as the body aligns prevents fishtailing off the shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Why does the first snowfall of the season demand extra defensive alertness?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: After months of dry summer grip, surrounding motorists tailgate and brake late until winter muscle memory returns.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Which four specific areas—along with the rest of your car—must be cleared of snow and ice before driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Roof snow slides onto windshields when braking, while crusted lamps, mirrors, and plates blind you and violate law.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Besides scraping all glass, which three exterior parts does Wisconsin explicitly tell you to brush clean?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Permit questions test whether you remember license plates and side mirrors alongside windows and exterior lights.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What two basic adjustments define safe everyday winter driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Cutting speed while stretching your front cushion gives snow tires room to slow smoothly without emergency stabs.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: What is Wisconsin's rule on using cruise control when pavement turns slick?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Cruise control adds throttle if spinning tires lose speed on ice, kicking the car sideways before you can tap off.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: Which headlight setting belongs on—and which stays off—in winter snow conditions?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Falling snowflakes bounce high-beam glare straight back into your eyes while low beams light the road and taillights.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: At least how many feet behind a flashing snowplow must you stay in Wisconsin?
