sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Swirling snow clouds behind a blade hide sudden stops, wing plows, and flying sand or salt.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: What are Wisconsin's two headline winter numbers and light rules—one for your beams and one for snowplows?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Keep your own high beams off in snow, and hold at least two hundred feet behind flashing plows.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: Which three flashing light colors on a snowplow trigger the two-hundred-foot following rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: State, county, and municipal plows run red, amber, or green beacons—all three demand the full two-hundred-foot buffer.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Which three slow or unpredictable hazards should you watch for on Wisconsin rural roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Cresting a country hill at fifty-five miles per hour leaves seconds to slow if farm machinery or cattle block the lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: Why might a tractor operator miss your car behind them, and what lights can towed farm gear lack?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Engine roar and wide implements block sound and mirrors while older wagons often carry zero turn or brake lamps.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: Why is whipping out to pass a slowing tractor near a field driveway risky?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Because towed implements often lack turn signals and brake lamps, a slowing tractor may swing left across your pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What attitude does the handbook call for when stuck behind wide, slow farm equipment?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Most farmers only travel short stretches between fields and pull aside as soon as a firm wide shoulder appears.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: Who holds the legal right-of-way when livestock are crossing or walking beside a Wisconsin highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Cattle and horses weigh a thousand pounds and bolt unpredictably, so state law gives animals on or near roads priority.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: Why must you keep off your horn near livestock, and what should you do instead?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Blasting a car horn spooks cattle or horses into bolting straight across your hood.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: What three behaviors combine when you encounter livestock on or along a rural highway?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Give animals full right-of-way, creep past with wide clearance, and stay silent so nothing panics the herd.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Below what age is it illegal to operate a farm tractor or self-propelled farm machine on a Wisconsin highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Public highway traffic demands mature judgment, barring anyone younger than sixteen from driving farm machinery on the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How do alcohol, drugs, and other impairing substances interfere with your thinking and traffic judgment?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Impaired thinking misjudges how fast nearby cars approach and how much gap remains before turning or braking.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Does Wisconsin's ban on drugged driving cover prescription medications and store-bought remedies too?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Pharmacy labels and store shelves never shield a driver when drowsiness or dizziness impairs safe vehicle control.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What happens to a driver's likelihood of crashing when driving drunk or drugged?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Slowed reactions and distorted gap judgment push collision odds sharply upward whenever alcohol or drugs enter driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What is Wisconsin's legal alcohol concentration limit for any driver under age twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Even one sip puts an underage driver above zero point zero zero percent and violates state law.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: How much of a controlled substance in your body counts legally as impaired driving in Wisconsin?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Wisconsin sets no safe threshold for controlled substances because any detectable trace in your system counts as impaired.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: Who is bound by the zero-alcohol rule compared with Wisconsin's zero-tolerance rule for controlled substances?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Don't mix up who gets zero tolerance because alcohol's zero limit targets under-twenty-one while controlled substances cover every age.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: According to research cited in the Wisconsin handbook, how does marijuana use affect driving performance?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Drivers who assume cannabis makes them extra cautious actually commit noticeably more behind-the-wheel errors in studies.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: What must you check before getting behind the wheel after taking a prescription or nonprescription medicine?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Scanning the bottle's side-effect warnings before starting the engine catches hidden drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reflexes.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: When a medication bottle warns against operating heavy machinery, what everyday activity is included?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: A multi-ton passenger car moving at street speed is heavy machinery, so stay out of the driver's seat.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Why doesn't having a doctor's prescription or store receipt make an impairing medicine legal to drive on?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Lawful possession only covers buying or taking the medicine at home, whereas driving impaired by any drug stays illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Which safe ride options does the Wisconsin handbook recommend if you have been drinking?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Lining up a sober friend, family member, or bartender-called cab gets you home without risking lives or arrest.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: What is the single thing capable of sobering a person up after drinking alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Coffee, cold showers, and fresh air only make an impaired person wide-awake drunk while the liver works slowly.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: Under Wisconsin's Implied Consent Law, how must you respond when an officer requests a PAC screening?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Driving on Wisconsin roads carries built-in legal agreement to submit whenever law enforcement requests alcohol concentration testing.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: What does a prohibited alcohol concentration check look for, and which two methods does it use?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Officers use either breath analysis or drawn blood to determine whether measurable alcohol sits in your bloodstream.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Which two specimen methods can make up a prohibited alcohol concentration check in Wisconsin?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Keep those two testing formats paired together because Wisconsin PAC screening relies on breathalyzer or blood analysis.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: What immediate action must a law enforcement officer take if you refuse a requested PAC test?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Saying no at the roadside leaves the officer zero discretion and requires arresting you under Implied Consent.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: For at least how long do you lose driving privileges after refusing a PAC test?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Refusing chemical testing strips away your driving privilege for twelve months minimum on top of additional penalties.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Why doesn't refusing an officer's PAC request work as a loophole to dodge trouble?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Trying to dodge breath or blood testing backfires immediately by triggering mandatory arrest and at least a yearlong loss.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Because distraction is dangerous, what should hold your mental focus and your gaze while driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Keeping both mental focus on vehicle control and eyes scanning down the road prevents split-second lane drift.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: What headphone or headset setup must you never wear while driving in Wisconsin?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Sealing off both ears with over-ear cans or dual earbuds blocks horns, screeching tires, and approaching sirens.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What real-world sound benchmark sets how loud you may play your car radio?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Blasting cabin speakers drowns out ambulances and fire trucks long before their flashing lights enter your mirrors.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: Contrast what Wisconsin restricts on headsets versus how it regulates your car stereo?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Headphone rules target covering both ears, whereas stereo guidance lets speakers play low enough to hear sirens.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: How should you handle an incoming phone call while driving, and what if taking it is unavoidable?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Letting calls go to voicemail keeps your attention forward until you can park safely off live lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Instead of picking up a ringing phone in moving traffic, what safe alternative does the handbook give?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Finding a safe spot off the roadway first separates phone attention completely from steering and braking.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Under what single circumstance may an instruction permit or probationary license holder use a cell phone while driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Novice drivers cannot even use hands-free chatter for casual calls; only reporting an emergency is allowed.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: What phone habit does the handbook urge for regular license holders, and how should necessary calls be placed?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Even experienced drivers lose reaction time on calls, so skip them when possible or route through hands-free.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: How do cell phone rules while driving compare between permit or probationary drivers and regular license holders?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Hands-free calling is never a loophole for permit or probationary drivers, who stay restricted strictly to emergencies.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: Where must your vehicle be before you read route directions or eat food?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Unfolding maps or unwrapping food steals both hands and sightlines, so stop safely off traffic first.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: Which two ways does the Wisconsin handbook recommend keeping a pet secure inside your car?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Keeping animals crated or held by a rider stops them from climbing onto your lap or pedals.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What two visibility-blocking decorations should you keep off your rearview mirror and vehicle windows?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Swinging mirror charms and window stickers create blind zones capable of hiding cyclists or pedestrians at intersections.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: What rule links reading directions with eating a meal during a road trip?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Treat route checking and snacking as parked-or-pulled-over errands rather than things to juggle at highway speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: What defines drowsy driving, and what causes it besides getting too little sleep?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Extreme fatigue hits not just after late nights, but also from untreated sleep disorders or marathon workdays.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: Even after spending hours in bed, which two factors can still leave a driver dangerously drowsy?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Don't assume bedtime hours tell the whole story when sleep apnea or exhausting shifts still cause microsleeps.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: Why is getting a full night's sleep before driving especially critical for teens and young adults?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Teens and young adults statistically suffer higher rates of fatigue-related crashes, making pre-trip rest essential.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: Which three physical or lane-keeping warning signs mean you must pull over and rest immediately?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Repeated blinking or yawning, wandering across lane lines, or buzzing edge rumble strips means sleep is winning.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: How should you treat drifting from your lane or striking the roadside rumble strip?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Crossing lane paint or vibrating on shoulder grooves demands pulling off to rest just like heavy yawning.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: What safety advantage do you gain by keeping wider distance from other road users?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Every extra car length gives your brain and brakes precious seconds when someone swerves or stops short.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: On a multi-lane road, how should you adjust speed instead of cruising right beside another vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Pacing door-to-door traps your escape lane and puts you squarely inside the other driver's side blind spot.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: How should you position your car near curbside parked vehicles and around blocked driver sightlines?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Extra clearance guards against swinging car doors while staying out of blocked sightlines prevents surprise pull-outs.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: Which two multi-lane positions should you avoid, and what single speed adjustment solves both?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Advancing slightly or easing back clears both side-by-side pacing and lingering where mirrors cannot spot you.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Which people near traffic need extra alertness and wider space buffers from drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Children darting into streets, walkers, lost motorists, and sight-blocked drivers can move unpredictably without warning.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Under Wisconsin law, what is the single legal exception to the ban on driving across a sidewalk?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Sidewalks belong strictly to pedestrians, allowing tires onto concrete only when pulling across into a driveway or alley.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and sirens?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Clearing toward the curb and staying completely stopped keeps emergency lanes open and predictable until responders pass.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Where must you never come to a stop when an emergency vehicle approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Freezing mid-intersection blocks turning fire trucks and ambulances from every cross-street direction.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: Contrast where yielding to an approaching emergency vehicle puts your car versus where you must never stop?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Always clear the intersection box first and tuck cleanly against the roadside curb before stopping.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: Which lane must you choose and hold when passing a stopped emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Shifting away from the adjacent lane and holding the farthest lane protects responders stepping beside traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: How does your legal duty change between a moving emergency vehicle and one stopped with flashing lights?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Rolling sirens require pulling roadside to a full stop, whereas parked flashing lights require vacating the adjacent lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What does Wisconsin law require when passing a police car stopped at the roadside with lights and siren active?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Giving roadside officers either an empty buffer lane or reduced speed prevents deadly shoulder strikes.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Which two legal options protect officers when a squad car sits stopped on the roadside?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: When traffic blocks you from shifting over a lane safely, dropping your speed fulfills Wisconsin's protection rule.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: At least how many feet away must you stop when a school bus flashes its red lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Stopping twenty feet or farther back leaves a visible safety zone where children cross ahead of the bumper.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: On an undivided roadway, which directions of traffic must stop for a school bus flashing red lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Students cross both lanes around an undivided bus stop, requiring following and oncoming drivers alike to halt.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: After stopping for a school bus, what must you watch for and when may you move again?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Creeping forward before the red lamps shut off risks hitting a late runner dashing toward the curb.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Pair the minimum stopping gap for a flashing school bus with the exact cue allowing you to proceed?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Hold at least twenty feet clear and stay planted until those alternating red flashers turn completely dark.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: When are oncoming drivers exempt from stopping for a school bus on the opposite side of the highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Only a physical barrier separating opposing directions lets opposite-side traffic keep moving past a flashing school bus.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Contrast who stops for a flashing school bus on an ordinary two-way street versus a barrier-divided highway?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Without a physical divider both directions stop, whereas a barrier-divided highway stops only traffic on the bus's side.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: Why must you leave extra following distance behind a motorcycle?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Because low-weight motorcycles decelerate far quicker than passenger cars, tailgating almost guarantees a rear-end strike.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: What weight-related braking trait explains why motorcycles need extra following space?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: A rider's light machine sheds speed rapidly, catching close-following cars without enough pavement to brake.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: What precautions should you take before changing lanes or passing around a motorcycle?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Narrow motorcycle profiles vanish easily behind roof pillars, making shoulder head-checks and patient passing critical.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: How much of a traffic lane is a bicyclist entitled to use, and may you squeeze alongside in that lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Cyclists legally command the entire travel lane to dodge potholes or debris, so never crowd beside them.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Why must you wait until oncoming traffic clears before overtaking a bicyclist?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: A rider dodging broken glass or sewer grates can swerve instantaneously into your path if you squeeze past.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: What minimum side clearance must you leave between your vehicle and a bicyclist when passing?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Passing closer than three feet buffets a rider with mirror wind-blast and leaves zero margin for wobble.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Which two conditions—side space and opposing lane status—must line up before you pass a bicyclist?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Wait until opposing traffic opens up completely so you can swing wide with three feet or more.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Why must drivers stay extra watchful for bicycles even though bikes are supposed to carry lights or reflectors?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Never assume every night cyclist has working reflectors or lamps; active visual scanning spots dark silhouettes early.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: What are truck no-zones, and roughly how far do they stretch behind and ahead of a large truck?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Tall cabs and long trailers create huge blind zones extending two hundred feet rearward and twenty feet forward.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: How does the length of a large truck's rear no-zone compare with its front no-zone?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: At roughly two hundred feet behind versus twenty feet ahead, tailgating a trailer hides you completely.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: In which close-in fore-and-aft spots around a big truck does your car disappear from the trucker's view?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Tucking right off a trailer bumper or cutting tight across the hood puts you outside every cab mirror.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: How should you clear out of a truck's no-zone, and how should you handle passing one?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Either accelerate ahead or ease back into mirror view, and never camp beside trailer tires while passing.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Pair the two ways to exit a truck's no-zone with the right pace when overtaking a rig?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Lingering alongside a semi invites lane-change squeezes, so clear the blind zone promptly once you commit.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Whenever an emergency leaves you or someone else injured, what is always step number one?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Getting paramedics and police rolling first saves critical minutes before exchanging details or checking sheet metal.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Are most traffic crashes unavoidable bad luck, or what habit lets you pick the right escape?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Spotting brake lights or drifting tires two seconds earlier opens up smooth braking or steering escapes.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: How much does a teen driver's crash risk jump when just one other teenager rides along?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Peer conversation, music, and showing off split novice attention enough to double collision odds immediately.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: How should you alert trailing drivers when you spot a vehicle stopped along the side of the road ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lamps several times wakes up following traffic before you ease speed or shift lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Why do you tap the brake pedal three or four times near a roadside vehicle instead of holding hard pressure?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Don't confuse warning taps with panic braking—flashing taillights communicate caution behind you rather than halting fast.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Which three maneuvers does the Wisconsin handbook give for avoiding an imminent crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Slamming brakes is not your only move—steering clear or accelerating out of a side hit often works faster.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: How do you brake for an emergency stop in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Keeping firm continuous foot pressure lets the ABS computer modulate each wheel rapidly until danger clears.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: What mechanical problem does ABS prevent during hard braking, and what is the result?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Rolling tires grip asphalt and steer around hazards, whereas locked tires slide straight ahead out of control.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: Why is pumping the brake pedal wrong during an emergency stop in an ABS-equipped car?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Lifting your foot resets the anti-lock pulsing cycle and stretches out your stopping distance right toward the hazard.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What collision hazard comes with making a sudden hard stop, and what habit guards against it?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Knowing whether a tailgater or heavy truck trails close behind helps you decide between hard braking and steering open.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How should you grip the wheel when swerving around a hazard, and what trap hits right afterward?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Yanking one-handed dodges the first bumper only to spin out of control into a guardrail or second car.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Why is clearing the initial obstacle only half the battle when you turn to avoid a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Weight transfer snaps back hard after a quick swerve, demanding steady hands so dodging one crash never starts another.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Where should your eyes and steering aim during an emergency dodge, and which lane is strictly off-limits?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Taking a grass shoulder or bush glances off energy, whereas swerving left into opposing traffic risks a fatal head-on.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: In which two impact angles can hitting the gas beat hitting the brakes, and what do you do once clear?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: When someone runs a cross-street stop or barrels up behind you, brisk acceleration clears your trunk before slowing safely.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: After accelerating ahead of a side or rear collision threat, what step completes the maneuver?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Bursting clear buys space from the side or rear strike, then easing speed keeps you from overrunning traffic ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: After a collision before responders arrive, what must you do about leaving and alerting oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Warning approaching cars immediately with four-way hazards or roadside flares prevents secondary pileups.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: When a crash injures or kills someone, what three rules govern nine-one-one, vehicle positions, and where you wait?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Preserving exact vehicle positions aids crash reconstruction while staying buckled inside shields you from passing lanes when safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: How does Wisconsin law treat driving away from a crash where someone was injured or killed?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Panicking and fleeing an injury collision turns an accident into a serious criminal hit-and-run prosecution.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: If nobody is hurt in a crash yet your car won't drive, what three steps keep you safe?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Standing between disabled bumpers in live lanes invites fatal secondary strikes—step well back off the roadway while waiting.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: When nobody is injured and your vehicle still drives safely after a minor crash, where do the cars belong?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Leaving drivable fender-benders parked mid-highway triggers worse secondary rear-end crashes behind the backup.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: In a zero-injury collision, how does your next step differ between a disabled car and a drivable one?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Move rolling cars onto a shoulder or lot first, or step clear and call nine-one-one if wheels are jammed.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: When do you leave crashed vehicles untouched in the road versus moving them to the side?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Exam questions test this exact boundary—injury or death freezes the scene, while unhurt drivable cars clear traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: Which three categories of details must you exchange with other drivers after a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Capturing license numbers, plate and make details, and insurance carriers ensures accurate claims and police reports.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Beyond driver documents, what three scene facts should you write down before memories fade?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Noting damage on every car, jotting down how impact unfolded, and saving witness contacts protects you if stories change.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Does any crash involving injury or death require a police report in Wisconsin?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Even seemingly minor neck or passenger pain requires notifying law enforcement for an official crash report.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: At what dollar amount of general property damage must a Wisconsin crash be reported to police?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Modern bumper sensors and paint easily pass one thousand dollars, making most dings beyond tiny scratches reportable.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: At what lower dollar threshold must you report crash damage to government property like signs or guardrails?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Bending a highway signpost or denting a guardrail triggers mandatory reporting at just two hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: How does Wisconsin's general property-damage reporting threshold compare with its government-property threshold?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Watch whether the test question mentions a private bumper or a public signpost—government damage drops the trigger fivefold.
