visual_sync.text_span: One thousand general, two hundred public

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: Besides injury and dollar damage, which two scene conditions legally require reporting a crash to police?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Tow-blocking wrecks and suspected alcohol or drug impairment always require an officer on scene regardless of repair cost.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: When must you still report a crash to police even with zero injuries and minor visible damage?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Never walk away from a light tap if a wheel is jammed or the other driver smells or acts impaired.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What are your first two safety actions in any roadside emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Summoning medical help for injuries and lighting four-way flashers right away protects everyone inside and approaching.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Which two controls do you work—and in what order—if your regular brakes suddenly fail?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Pumping several times may rebuild hydraulic pressure in dual-circuit lines before mechanical parking-brake cables slow the rear wheels.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: While slowing with the parking brake after brake failure, what must you do if the car starts skidding?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Parking brakes clamp only rear wheels—locking them spins the tail out unless you release tension and coast safely.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What is the complete three-part rule for handling failed brakes without spinning out?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Try pumping main brakes before pulling the parking brake, and stay ready on the release button if rear tires slide.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Which four calm steps bring your car safely off the road after a sudden tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Fighting the tug straight while easing off the gas lets speed bleed down gradually before pulling onto firm ground.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: If your engine quits while rolling, what do you do with the ignition key and what steering change will you feel?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Leaving the key in On avoids locking the steering column while you muscle heavy unassisted steering onto the shoulder.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: Why does steering suddenly take much more arm strength right after an engine stalls?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Your steering linkage still works mechanically, so pull firmly with both hands instead of thinking steering broke.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What switch check and backup lights help you pull off safely if your headlights go out?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Cycling the switch off and back on checks whether only parking lamps were selected while hazard flashers mark your exit.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: What four-step sequence stops a vehicle safely when the gas pedal sticks down?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Shifting to Neutral disconnects runaway engine power immediately while keeping power steering alive until you park off-road.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: Why do you leave the key in On during a stalled engine and wait until parked off-road to turn off a stuck-gas engine?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: In both emergencies, the engine only turns off after stopping off-road so your steering wheel never locks mid-lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: How does your first move for a stuck gas pedal differ from your first move for a tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: A stuck throttle needs Neutral to sever engine drive, whereas a blown tire needs straight-wheel coasting off the gas.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What credential is required to drive on Wisconsin public roads, and which four tests lead to it?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Unlike states that combine signs into one written bank, Wisconsin breaks highway signs out into its own standalone check.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: What does Wisconsin's vision screening measure, and which two providers may conduct it?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Having your own eye specialist complete the vision check ahead of time saves time at the service counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: What minimum visual acuity score applies to regular car and motorcycle applicants, and are lenses permitted?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Reaching twenty over forty in at least one eye qualifies, whether naturally or while wearing glasses or contacts.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: How many degrees of side vision must Wisconsin applicants show, and from where is it measured?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Side vision measured outward from the center of each eye spots cross-street cars and cyclists early.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How do Wisconsin's twenty-over-forty acuity standard and seventy-degree field standard differ in eye coverage?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Written questions love testing that sharpness requires only one qualifying eye while side width checks each eye.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Does needing prescription glasses or contacts to hit twenty over forty count against you during screening?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Wearing your prescription simply adds a corrective-lens notation rather than failing the vision screening.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Which three functional categories of road signs does Wisconsin's highway signs test evaluate?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Missing any one group among regulatory rules, hazard warnings, or route directions costs easy points.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: How many questions appear on Wisconsin's highway signs test, and what score passes it?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: With only fifteen questions on screen, missing more than three drops you below the eighty-percent mark.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Must you reserve an appointment ahead of time to take Wisconsin's highway signs test?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Walk-in access lets you clear your highway signs check during normal DMV service center hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: How much of the Wisconsin handbook's sign coverage does the DMV advise studying beforehand?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Any sign category in the manual is fair game among your fifteen random highway-sign questions.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What subject does Wisconsin's knowledge test measure, and is an advance appointment required?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Like the signs check, the traffic-law exam accepts walk-in applicants without prior scheduling.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: How many total questions make up Wisconsin's knowledge test, and how many right answers pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Forty out of fifty gives you a ten-question cushion before dipping under eighty percent.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: What passing percentage links Wisconsin's two written tests, and how do their raw numbers differ?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Keeping twelve-of-fifteen paired with forty-of-fifty anchors both written cutoffs under one eighty-percent rule.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How does the focus of Wisconsin's highway signs test differ from the focus of its knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Splitting sign recognition from statutory driving rules ensures learners master both before getting a permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Roughly how long does Wisconsin's knowledge test take, and when must you arrive before closing?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Walking into a DMV branch fifteen minutes before closing leaves too little time to finish fifty questions.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: Why does the Wisconsin handbook remind walk-in applicants not to start the knowledge test late in the afternoon?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Budgeting three-quarters of an hour keeps you from rushing answers against the service center's closing bell.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: What is the fee to take written tests at a Wisconsin DMV service center, and where can you practice free?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Using the official DMV website's zero-cost sample quiz preps you before walking into a branch for free.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Which age group may take Wisconsin's knowledge test online from home, and what fee applies?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Younger teens can trade a branch trip for a ten-dollar online exam session.
sec01-card-sec01-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Ages fifteen to seventeen, ten dollars

visual_sync.text_span: Ages fifteen to seventeen, ten dollars

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Contrast the cost of taking Wisconsin's written tests in person at a DMV center versus online?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: In-branch signs and knowledge testing costs nothing, whereas the optional teen home exam charges ten dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: Can adult applicants aged eighteen and up use the paid online knowledge test described in the handbook?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Only fifteen-to-seventeen-year-olds qualify for the ten-dollar online knowledge option; older applicants test at a center.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: What other names refer to the skills test, and what basic ability does it prove behind the wheel?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Examiners look for calm, everyday safe control rather than stunt driving during your road evaluation.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: Which three terms does Wisconsin use interchangeably for the in-car exam with a DMV examiner?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Whether a form or web page says road test, driving test, or skills test, all three mean the exact same drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Who rides beside you during the skills test, and how do they guide your route and maneuvers?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Clear spoken instructions tell you well ahead when to turn at the next corner or perform a Y-turn.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: How does booking the Wisconsin skills test differ from walking in for the written tests?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Showing up unscheduled works only for written exams because road-test slots must be booked online first.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: Group Wisconsin's signs, knowledge, and skills tests by which allow walk-ins versus require online booking?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Keeping signs and knowledge in the walk-in column and skills in the online-appointment column prevents wasted trips.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: What six vehicle items does the DMV examiner inspect before your skills test leaves the lot?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: A dead brake bulb, missing plate, or stuck door ends your appointment curbside before scoring even begins.
sec01-card-sec01-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Horn, lights, signals, plates, doors, mirrors

visual_sync.text_span: Horn, lights, signals, plates, doors, mirrors

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: Why can an applicant who practiced every driving maneuver still get turned away before starting the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Examiners verify horn, lights, blinkers, tags, doors, and mirrors first so nobody tests in an unsafe car.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: Which three cabin visibility controls does the handbook say you should know how to work effortlessly?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Fumbling across unfamiliar stalks if rain starts or glass fogs pulls your eyes off traffic mid-drive.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: Why should you locate the headlight, wiper, and defrost switches before starting a road test in a borrowed car?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Operating basic visibility controls smoothly is a core part of road-test readiness rather than an afterthought.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Along with turning, which two contrasting kinds of intersections are graded during Wisconsin's skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Examiners watch both crisp full halts at stop signs and active left-right scanning through uncontrolled corners.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: Do Wisconsin examiners grade only intersections with stop signs and red lights, or through approaches too?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: Floating blindly past open side streets without scanning drops points just like rolling a stop line.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: Beyond turns and intersections, what three traffic environments or movements are scored on the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Handling business or residential streets, clean mirror-and-shoulder lane shifts, and straight reversing rounds out traffic scoring.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: Which three specific low-speed maneuvers appear on Wisconsin's skills test and deserve advance practice?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Rehearsing three-point Y-turns, curb pull-overs, and clean parking prevents curb bumps under pressure.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.question_text: How is the Y-turn highlighted twice in Wisconsin's overview of the driving skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.teaching_text: Featuring the Y-turn both as a sample examiner command and as a graded maneuver underscores practicing it well.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: Where can you read extra Wisconsin skills-test prep tips, and what rehearsal rule does the handbook stress?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Drilling every single listed skill beforehand turns exam day into muscle memory.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Which license class covers standard noncommercial driving of cars and light trucks in Wisconsin?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Knowing Class D stands for everyday passenger cars and pickups separates regular licensing from heavy commercial classes.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Where do you apply for a Wisconsin license, and what documents prove your full name and birth date?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: First-time license applications happen face-to-face at a DMV service center with official birth or passport records.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Alongside name and birth date, what legal standing must you document, and which same item can cover it?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Bringing your U.S. birth certificate or valid passport checks off both birth details and citizenship in one move.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: How many Wisconsin residency documents must you present, what examples qualify, and what number is required?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Showing up with only one utility bill or bank statement stalls your application when two Wisconsin address proofs are mandatory.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Contrast how one birth certificate or passport works for birth and status against what Wisconsin residency requires?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: A single passport handles name, birthday, and citizenship, yet residency always demands two separate Wisconsin address items.
sec02-card-sec02-R01.must_match_memory_hook: One covers status; address needs two

visual_sync.text_span: One covers status; address needs two

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: Which two common cards satisfy Wisconsin's proof-of-identity requirement at the DMV counter?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Remembering to sign your Social Security card before arriving lets it satisfy identity verification cleanly.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Why are photocopies or expired IDs turned away at the DMV, and what non-paperwork standards apply?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Staff reject copies and expired cards on sight while also confirming applicants meet physical and medical standards.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: Who must sign a minor's Wisconsin Driver License Application, and what form number is it?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: No applicant under eighteen can move forward at the counter without an eligible adult signature on form MV3001.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: What legal and financial responsibility does an adult sponsor take on, and can they cancel it later?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Because crashes caused by the minor fall financially on the sponsor, Wisconsin lets sponsors pull backing whenever needed.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: What school-standing facts does a sponsor certify upfront, and what driving record do they sign off on later?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Habitual truancy blocks teen licensing, and the same sponsor later attests that supervised practice hours happened.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Through what license stage and until what birthday does adult sponsorship remain active?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Passing the road test does not end adult liability because sponsorship stays attached until the teen's eighteenth birthday.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: Which four household or exchange-program adults qualify to sponsor a teen living with family?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Wisconsin includes host parents of foreign exchange students right alongside parents, step-parents, and legal guardians.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: When a minor lives apart from parents or guardians, which six relatives or foster adults may sponsor?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Living outside a parent's home opens sponsorship to grandparents, aunts, uncles, foster parents, or adult siblings and spouses.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: Among extended-family sponsors, which two must be at least eighteen while the others carry no stated age floor?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Exam questions single out siblings and spouses because they alone carry an explicit eighteen-or-older rule.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: Which independent or bereaved minors may file proof of insurance in place of an adult sponsor?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Minors with no living parent or living apart while working or studying full-time substitute insurance filings.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Which two additional groups of minors can substitute proof of insurance for an adult sponsor?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: State, county, or court wards in care and minors married to someone under eighteen qualify with insurance proof.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: Contrast replacing a sponsor through proof of insurance against using an extended-family relative as sponsor?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Independent or ward minors bypass needing a signer via insurance, whereas relatives sign MV3001 and take liability.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: Why must beginners get an instruction permit first, and which three checks qualify an applicant eighteen or older?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Adults eighteen and up skip driver-ed enrollment rules and earn a permit straight from passing all three counter checks.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: Beyond passing vision, signs, and knowledge, what age floor and course rule apply to permit seekers under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Teens cannot pick up an instruction permit until turning fifteen and enrolling in classroom plus behind-the-wheel training.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: What separates the instruction-permit requirements for someone under eighteen from someone eighteen or older?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Both groups pass knowledge, signs, and vision, leaving age fifteen and driver-ed enrollment as teen-only extras.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: What signed form must a teen's behind-the-wheel driving school provide before the teen applies for a permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Arriving at the DMV before your driving school signs MV3001 leaves your teen permit packet incomplete.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Which two separate parties sign form MV3001 along a Wisconsin teen's path to an instruction permit?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Connecting both your adult sponsor and your behind-the-wheel school to form MV3001 locks in that form number.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: May a Class D permit holder ever drive solo, and what license status and experience must their mentor have?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Supervising companions must hold a full regular license for two years rather than a probationary or occupational card.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: Why do probationary and occupational licenses fail to qualify someone to supervise a Wisconsin permit driver?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Even with two years behind the wheel, someone on an occupational or probationary card cannot legally supervise.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: Where must the supervising companion sit, and what minimum ages apply across instructors, family, and others?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Qualified instructors, parents, guardians, and spouses qualify at nineteen, whereas anyone else needs twenty-one.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: Which supervising companions qualify at age nineteen on a permit, and who must be at least twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: A twenty-year-old friend or coworker misses the twenty-one cutoff even though a nineteen-year-old spouse or instructor qualifies.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: Under what front-seat supervision condition may a permit driver carry immediate family in the back seat?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Siblings can ride along in back only when a parent, guardian, or spouse occupies the front passenger seat.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: Before a minor permit holder drives with a qualified adult aged twenty-one or older, what consent is required?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Verbal approval is not enough if an officer checks why a twenty-one-plus family friend is supervising.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: Once a permit holder is sixteen, what single extra non-family passenger may ride in a rear seat?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Only one experienced twenty-five-plus licensed driver may occupy a non-front seat alongside your front mentor.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: Compare the youngest possible age of a front-seat permit mentor with an extra licensed rider in back?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Keeping nineteen upfront separate from twenty-five in back prevents mixing Wisconsin's two permit passenger tiers.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: Who must sit in the front passenger seat whenever a permit holder practices driving in darkness?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Nighttime hazards raise the companion bar to twenty-five with two years' experience unless riding with an instructor.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: Which Wisconsin license is issued right after passing the skills test, and what is its minimum age?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Every newly tested driver starts on a probationary card once reaching at least sixteen years old.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: Under what sole exception may someone driving on a Wisconsin probationary license use a phone?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Even hands-free chatting or music tapping is barred on a probationary license outside genuine emergency calls.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: What permit tenure, birthday, and course proof must an applicant under eighteen have before getting a probationary license?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Waiting to get your permit past fifteen-and-a-half pushes your probationary date past your sixteenth birthday.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: Why is turning sixteen by itself not enough to qualify a teen for a Wisconsin probationary license?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: All three pieces, sixteen years old, six permit months, and completed driver ed, must line up together.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: How many supervised practice hours must a permit holder log, and how do day and dark hours divide?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Logging forty daylight hours alongside ten after-dark hours builds round-the-clock experience with a qualified adult.
sec02-card-sec02-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Fifty hours; forty day, ten dark

visual_sync.text_span: Fifty hours; forty day, ten dark

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: Can fifty hours of bright-daylight driving satisfy Wisconsin's supervised permit practice rule?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Even sixty sunny hours leave you short until at least ten logged hours take place after dark.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: Is fifty hours a cap or a floor, and who verifies both the total and after-dark hours?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Many teens need extra practice beyond fifty hours before their sponsor signs off on road-test readiness.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: Which two tools can Wisconsin sponsors use to record a teen's supervised practice hours?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Tracking drives on paper or inside the RoadReady app keeps daytime and darkness totals organized.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: What is another name for a teen probationary license, who faces its limits, and why?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Extra teen friends and late-night fatigue drive new-driver crashes, so GDL limits shield under-eighteen beginners.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: How long do initial GDL passenger and curfew restrictions last, and is a new card needed afterward?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Restrictions lift automatically after nine clean months or turning eighteen without visiting a DMV counter.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: From five a.m. to midnight, where may a GDL teen drive solo and how many immediate family members may ride?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Daytime and evening GDL rules place zero destination limits on solo drives or immediate family rides.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: From five a.m. to midnight, which non-family passengers may ride with a GDL driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Carrying two friends without a qualifying licensed adult breaks Wisconsin's one-other-passenger daytime cap.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.question_text: Contrast how daytime GDL passenger limits treat immediate family members versus non-family peers?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.teaching_text: Siblings never count against your one-friend slot, whereas packing multiple peers in back violates GDL.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: Between midnight and five a.m., between which three destinations may a GDL teen drive solo?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Late-night social runs are off-limits solo between midnight and five a.m. outside school or work commutes.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.question_text: What passenger limit applies to a GDL driver during the midnight-to-five-a.m. window?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.teaching_text: Having a qualified licensed adult with two years' experience beside you keeps overnight travel legal.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: How do solo GDL trip destinations change when the clock strikes midnight until five a.m.?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Open solo destinations from five a.m. to midnight narrow strictly to home, school, and work overnight.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.question_text: Which three record events extend a teen's GDL restrictions, and by how many months?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.teaching_text: Breaking passenger or curfew limits, or getting any moving ticket or suspension, tacks six more restricted months on.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.question_text: Compare the normal length of Wisconsin GDL restrictions with the length added after a violation?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.teaching_text: Keeping nine initial months distinct from the six-month penalty extension nails a favorite Wisconsin GDL question.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.question_text: What happens to demerit points on a second or later traffic conviction while holding a permit or probationary license?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.teaching_text: Doubled points pile up fast enough on a second ticket to trigger a rapid license suspension.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.question_text: At what birthday do Wisconsin's GDL passenger and night-hour restrictions end completely?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.teaching_text: Turning eighteen lifts teen curfew and passenger caps even if an earlier extension had not finished.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.question_text: What license stage follows Wisconsin's probationary license, and how early can you renew into it?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.teaching_text: Opening the upgrade window ninety days ahead lets you switch into a regular license before expiry.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.question_text: How often is a Wisconsin regular license renewed, how early may you renew, and where?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.teaching_text: Eligible drivers can renew online or at a DMV center up to twelve months before expiration.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.question_text: Compare how early you can renew a regular license against upgrading from probationary to regular?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.teaching_text: Probationary upgrades open ninety days out, whereas ongoing eight-year regular renewals open a full year ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.question_text: When does Wisconsin send out your driver license renewal reminder?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.teaching_text: Watching for notice a month and a half before your expiry-year birthday prevents driving on an expired card.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.question_text: Within how many days of moving to Wisconsin should a new resident transfer an out-of-state regular license?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.teaching_text: Waiting past two months after establishing Wisconsin residency leaves your old state card overdue for transfer.

sec02-card-sec02-F43.question_text: How soon after moving to Wisconsin must a commercial driver license holder apply for a Wisconsin CDL?
sec02-card-sec02-F43.teaching_text: Commercial drivers face half the grace window of regular motorists when switching state credentials.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.question_text: Contrast Wisconsin's new-resident license transfer window for a regular license versus a commercial CDL?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.teaching_text: Pairing sixty days for Class D against thirty days for CDL keeps both move-in clocks sharp.

sec02-card-sec02-F44.question_text: If your old state license already had a REAL ID star, does that status transfer automatically to Wisconsin?
sec02-card-sec02-F44.teaching_text: Federal verification rules require Wisconsin DMV staff to inspect all original REAL ID proofs fresh.

sec02-card-sec02-F45.question_text: Whose federal standards does a REAL ID satisfy, and what symbol marks a compliant Wisconsin card?
sec02-card-sec02-F45.teaching_text: Spotting the corner star confirms your license meets Department of Homeland Security verification rules.

sec02-card-sec02-F46.question_text: Starting May seven, two thousand twenty-five, which trips and facilities require a REAL ID or passport?
sec02-card-sec02-F46.teaching_text: Standard non-star licenses still cover driving, yet airport checkpoints and federal gates demand compliant ID.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.question_text: What symbol marks a REAL ID license, and what common travel document works in its place for domestic flights?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.teaching_text: Travelers without a star-marked license can still board domestic flights and enter federal sites using a passport.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Why does Wisconsin favor roundabouts, and which direction does traffic always travel inside one?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Eliminating head-on and T-bone intersection angles cuts serious crashes while keeping cars flowing counterclockwise around the center.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: What guides your lane selection approaching a roundabout, and how do left, middle, and right lanes usually divide turns?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Picking the right lane early from overhead arrows prevents panic weaves—left turns left, right exits right, middle goes straight.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Before reaching the yield line of a roundabout, what speed change do you make and whom do you yield to first?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Pedestrians and bicyclists cross the approach apron before you ever reach circulating motor traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: At the entrance to a roundabout, which direction of circulating traffic—and what large vehicle—must you yield to?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Circulating cars arrive from your left, and long semitruck trailers straddle extra space to clear the curve.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: Which four road users get priority before you pull into a Wisconsin roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Missing any one of those four—crosswalk walkers, cyclists, wide-tracking semis, or circulating left traffic—invites an entry collision.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: When do you pull into a roundabout, and must you come to a full stop if the circle is empty?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Treating an empty yield line like a four-way stop causes rear-end taps—glide smoothly in whenever nobody is circulating.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How does your entry move change between a busy roundabout and a completely empty one?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Yielding adapts to real traffic—hold for a clean gap when cars circulate, or keep rolling smoothly when clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Which three speed and lane rules apply once your car is circulating inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Changing lanes mid-circle cuts straight across spiraling exit paths where side mirrors struggle to spot adjacent cars.
sec07-card-sec07-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Low speed, hold lane, never switch

visual_sync.text_span: Low speed, hold lane, never switch

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What blinker move tells waiting drivers you are about to leave the roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Flashing your right blinker lets drivers waiting at the next leg know they have a gap instead of guessing.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Even if your overall route turned left through the roundabout, which turn signal marks your exit?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Every exit peels right off the counterclockwise ring, so a right turn signal is always the exit cue.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: What should you do if an emergency vehicle running its siren enters a roundabout before you pull in?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Staying out on the approach shoulder keeps the narrow curved ring completely open for the responder.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: If you are already inside a roundabout when an emergency vehicle approaches, why must you exit before pulling over?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Parking next to a curved center island chokes the narrow lane and traps the fire truck or ambulance behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does yielding to a siren-lit responder change once you have already entered a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether you know never to park inside the circle—clear out the next right exit first.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Which two legal options does a bicyclist have for navigating a one-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Confident riders take the slow circulating lane like a car, while others step onto the perimeter path and crosswalks.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: At a roundabout crosswalk, which way do pedestrians look from the curb versus from the center island?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Traffic approaches the entry leg from the left and exits past the splitter island from the walker's right.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Why does a pedestrian's head check flip from left at the curb to right on the roundabout island?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Splitter islands break crossing into two one-way stages, reversing which side cars come from at the halfway point.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What two steps are critical before pulling into a two-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: An inner-lane car spiraling toward the next exit crosses right across the outer entry path.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: When entering the right lane of a two-lane roundabout, why isn't checking only the outside lane enough?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Drivers in the inside lane legally exit across the outside lane, causing sideswipes if an entering car jumps in.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: In a two-lane roundabout, which lane handles left turns and U-turns, right turns, and going straight?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Left and U-turns belong inside, immediate rights stay outside, and straight-through drivers follow posted lane arrows.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Why should you check pavement arrows and overhead boards when going straight through a two-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Depending on exit geometry, straight-through traffic may use left, right, or both lanes—only the approach markings confirm.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How may a bicyclist pass through a two-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Even on two-lane circles, cyclists can either occupy a full traffic lane or exit onto the sidewalk and crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: What is the purpose of traffic signals placed on freeway entrance ramps?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Releasing one car at a time breaks up tight ramp platoons so freeway right-lane traffic keeps moving smoothly.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: How can you tell as you enter an on-ramp whether its ramp meter signals are currently operating?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Ramp meters often shut down outside rush hours, switching on their flashing warning board whenever active.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: Where must your front tires stop at an active ramp meter, and what happens if you stop short?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Stopping a car length back misses the buried loop detector, leaving the ramp signal stuck on red.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Why does the Wisconsin handbook emphasize pulling all the way up to a ramp meter's white stop line?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Pavement sensors sit right behind the painted bar and need your tires over them to cycle the light green.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: On a two-lane metered on-ramp, how do the signals work and when do you merge?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Side-by-side ramp lanes alternate greens so two cars do not race neck-and-neck toward the merge taper.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: What tells you a multi-lane ramp meter is running, and whose green light clears you to go?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Check the lit warning placard on entry, then watch strictly your own lane's signal head rather than your neighbor's.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Are ramp meter red lights optional suggestions, or what happens if you blow through one?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Ramp meters are enforceable traffic control signals—blowing past a red light carries a citation just like street intersections.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: What three benefits does a diverging diamond interchange deliver, and how do you navigate it?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Temporary crossover lanes eliminate left turns across opposing traffic—simply trust the overhead signals, arrows, and lane stripes.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Why do highway engineers build diverging diamond interchanges, and what keeps drivers in the right spot?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Clear lane lines, islands, and signals guide you effortlessly through a layout built for fewer crashes, less crowding, and lower cost.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: What overarching goal guides law enforcement, and what three possibilities might an officer investigate during a stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Understanding that officers check for emergencies, criminal leads, or routine traffic issues helps keep roadside interactions calm.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: Which side of the roadway should you pull onto when patrol lights flash behind you?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Pulling onto the right shoulder gives the officer space away from fast left-lane passing traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Right after pulling to the shoulder for a police stop, what three things do you do with your shifter, engine, and audio?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Securing Park prevents rollaways while shutting off the engine and stereo ensures clear, calm communication.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: During a traffic stop, what should you do regarding staying inside, your seat belt, and your window?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Unbuckling early makes it look like you could not wait—or weren't wearing your belt before pulling over.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: Should you step out of your car to walk back and meet the officer during a traffic stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Popping your door open surprises the approaching officer and exposes both of you to passing shoulder traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Where should you rest your hands during a traffic stop, and what movements should you avoid?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Rummaging in a dark glovebox before the officer asks looks risky—keep both hands visible atop the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: If you think a traffic ticket is unfair, how should you act roadside and where do you make your case?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Officers do not cancel written citations on the shoulder—save your explanation calmly for the judge.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: What is the proper place to contest a traffic citation in Wisconsin?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Roadside debates only lengthen time spent beside fast traffic, whereas traffic court exists specifically to review contested tickets.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: During what daily window are deer most active along Wisconsin roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Twilight and nighttime feeding patterns peak right when driver sightlines shrink to headlight range.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What visual clue gives away deer near dark roadsides, and what three actions should follow?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Headlight beams glint off deer eyes in ditches before bodies show—drop speed, sound your horn, and cover the brake.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: Why shouldn't you relax after one deer bounds clear, or assume city streets are deer-free?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Deer travel in groups and wander into suburbs and city parks at any hour of the year.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: Once you slow and honk for a deer's glowing eyes, why must you keep scanning after it clears?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Accelerating right behind the lead deer often puts your bumper into the second or third animal sprinting to catch up.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: If you hit a deer, what mechanical check comes first, and what details should you write down?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Leaking coolant or bent fenders can disable your car miles later, and exact crash notes streamline insurance claims.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: Under Wisconsin rules, who gets first claim to keep a vehicle-struck deer, and who is second in line?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Wisconsin allows salvage of road-struck venison—first to the driver involved, then to the next passing motorist if declined.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: Why must you phone police after striking a deer whether you keep it or leave it behind?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Keeping the deer requires an official police possession tag, and leaving it requires reporting its roadside spot for removal.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: Does declining to keep a deer you hit excuse you from calling law enforcement?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Unreported carcasses left near lanes cause secondary swerve crashes, so police need the location even when you skip the tag.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: How does the Wisconsin handbook define a funeral procession?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Recognizing a formal procession traveling from a service to a cemetery or crematorium cues other motorists to give respectful right-of-way.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: In a Wisconsin funeral procession, what rule binds the first vehicle, and what must every vehicle in line turn on?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: The lead car waits for green lights and stop clearance first, while lit headlights mark every trailing car in the convoy.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: Which requirement applies solely to the lead vehicle of a funeral procession versus every car in line?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Once the lead vehicle enters legally on a green signal, continuous lit headlights show cross traffic the unbroken line.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: What is the rule for outside drivers encountering a moving funeral procession?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Splitting a lit procession causes confusion and rear-end hazards among unfamiliar out-of-town drivers following closely.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: At what point total does every Wisconsin driving record begin, and what adds demerit points?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Every driver starts with a clean zero-point slate until traffic court convictions begin stacking demerit points.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Which three driver groups face doubled demerit points, and on which conviction does doubling start?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Probationary, ID-only, and unlicensed drivers take normal points once, then double points from ticket two onward.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: Do probationary, ID-card, or unlicensed drivers get doubled points on their very first traffic conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Watch that classic first-ticket trap because point doubling kicks in only on conviction number two and beyond.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Accumulating how many demerit points within what rolling timeframe suspends or revokes your driving privilege?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Two doubled tickets on a probationary license can easily hit twelve points inside a year and sideline you.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: What five-year conviction totals—major or minor—classify a driver as a habitual traffic offender?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Rack up four major convictions or twelve minor ones across five years and habitual-offender status hits.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How does Wisconsin's twelve-point loss rule differ from habitual-offender status in both unit counted and timeframe?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Separate those two clocks cleanly because twelve-month tracking counts demerit points whereas five-year tracking counts convictions.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Within a five-year span, compare how many major convictions versus minor convictions trigger habitual-offender status?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Major violations carry triple the weight toward habitual status, needing just four convictions compared with twelve minor ones.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Where can you check exact demerit point values and see whether an offense counts as major or minor?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Wisconsin publishes its full point schedule and major-versus-minor violation classifications online through the DMV portal.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: How long is a habitual traffic offender's privilege revoked, and how long before occupational eligibility may open?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Habitual offender status revokes regular driving five full years and blocks any occupational petition for two years.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: For a habitual traffic offender, contrast the full revocation term against the waiting period for a possible occupational license?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Keep five years tied to the underlying revocation and two years tied to earliest possible occupational relief.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Which five actions can take away your Wisconsin driving privilege, and must you hold a Wisconsin license first?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Even out-of-state or unlicensed motorists can have Wisconsin driving privileges suspended, revoked, canceled, disqualified, or denied.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Before applying for an occupational license, what should you check online and what proof must you present?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Confirming online eligibility first and bringing financial-responsibility proof prevents wasted trips to the service counter.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: What daily and weekly driving-hour ceilings govern a Wisconsin occupational license?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Driving outside your approved twelve-hour day or sixty-hour week violates the strict terms of occupational relief.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Can driving twelve hours every day of the week stay legal under an occupational license?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Seven twelve-hour days would hit eighty-four hours, busting the sixty-hour weekly cap that applies simultaneously.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Which everyday destinations—including two household examples—are permitted on an occupational license?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Occupational driving covers commuting to work or classes plus essential household needs like groceries and doctor visits.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: Beyond work, school, and household errands, which assessment and safety-plan trips does an occupational license cover?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Wisconsin lets occupational holders drive to the agency managing their Intoxicated Driver Program assessment and Driver Safety Plan.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: Once your revocation term finishes, which three steps reinstate your Wisconsin driver license?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Privilege never restores automatically when time expires; you must show identity, pay reinstatement, and file required insurance.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: While both may require financial responsibility proof, which two items does the handbook list specifically for reinstating a revoked license?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Keep full post-revocation reinstatement distinct by pairing financial responsibility with identity documents and a reinstatement fee.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: What format and language accommodations are offered for Wisconsin's knowledge and highway signs tests, and where are languages listed?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Applicants can listen via audio or choose among many translated languages posted on the DMV website.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: Which disclosure form and three delivery methods let you notify the DMV about an invisible disability?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Sending the voluntary Invisible Disability Disclosure form by email, mail, or fax records helpful context ahead of stops.
sec12-card-sec12-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Disclosure form via email, mail, fax

visual_sync.text_span: Disclosure form via email, mail, fax

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: Which two groups of personnel have access to an invisible disability disclosure filed with Wisconsin?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Limiting access to law enforcement officers and WisDOT staff helps roadside interactions stay informed and private.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What health conditions must you report to the DMV, and which standard license form lets you report them?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Disclosing medical conditions that could affect safe control right on your license application keeps evaluations straightforward.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: How do the Wisconsin forms differ between reporting a driving-related medical condition and disclosing an invisible disability?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Health conditions go on the regular driver license application whereas invisible disabilities use their own separate disclosure form.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: How can Wisconsin citizens missing standard paperwork obtain a free identification card for voting?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Pairing the ID application with the Administrator Petition lets eligible citizens get voting identification at zero charge.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: What practical benefit does the voting ID petition deliver before election day arrives?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: While underlying birth records are verified, the petition process issues valid voting documentation before polls close.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: What minimum age and citizenship requirement must you meet to start Wisconsin's voting ID petition process?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Seventeen-year-old U.S. citizens turning eighteen by the general election can start their voting ID petition early.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: Which five categories of available proof or personal info should you bring when starting a voting ID petition?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Bring whatever you hold showing name and birth date, identity, Wisconsin residency, U.S. citizenship, and Social Security number.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: Who must wear a seat belt inside a motor vehicle under Wisconsin law?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Wisconsin enforces universal belt use across every seat and every age group inside the cabin.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: Does Wisconsin's mandatory seat belt law let adult back-seat passengers ride unbuckled?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Unbelted back-seat adults become dangerous cabin projectiles in a crash and violate Wisconsin's all-ages belt statute.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: In what three ways does wearing a seat belt protect you while driving or during an impact?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Belts hold you behind the wheel during swerves, soften interior impacts, and keep you inside the cabin.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: When should you fasten your seat belt, and what should you verify for everyone riding with you?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Clicking belts while rolling steals focus from traffic, so secure yourself and every rider while still parked.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: Does driving a vehicle equipped with air bags excuse you from wearing a seat belt?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Air bags are engineered to work together with seat belts and can injure an unrestrained occupant.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: Across which exact body areas should your lap belt and shoulder belt rest?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Anchoring the lap strap across strong hip bones below your stomach prevents severe internal crash injuries.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: How much slack fits properly at your chest, and what two shoulder-belt positions are unsafe?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Allowing at most a fist at your chest works only when the strap stays squarely over your shoulder.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: Contrast how the lap strap and the shoulder strap fit properly across your body?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Keep the lap portion snug across your hip bones while giving the chest strap roughly a fist's room.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: Generally, until what ages do children ride in a child safety seat and then a booster seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Young riders generally stay harnessed in a child seat to age four before using a booster to eight.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Put Wisconsin's two general child-restraint stages in sequence along with each stage's age milestone?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Graduating a toddler into a booster before age four or adult belts before eight rushes crash protection.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: Where should you look to confirm proper belt routing and height-and-weight limits for a child safety seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Every car seat routes belts differently and sets specific size ceilings printed inside its manufacturer instruction booklet.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: What type of auto insurance must you carry in Wisconsin, and when must you show proof?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Driving without active liability coverage or failing to display proof during a traffic stop brings citations.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: Who must issue a Wisconsin resident's policy, and what insurance proof may out-of-state visitors show?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Residents need coverage from a Wisconsin-approved carrier, while visiting drivers can present valid home-state policies.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: When you get behind the wheel of a friend's or relative's vehicle, whose job is verifying it has insurance?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Saying it isn't my car will not stop a ticket if you drive an uninsured borrowed vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: Contrast Wisconsin's insurance rule for out-of-state motorists with the rule for driving someone else's car?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Visitors may show home-state carrier cards, yet anyone borrowing another person's car remains responsible for verifying coverage.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Which travel choices and trip-timing habits help cut down on fuel consumption?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Carpooling, ridesharing, biking, riding buses, walking, and skipping congested rush-hour traffic all trim fuel costs.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: How does stop-and-go driving affect your car compared with easing off speed gradually?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Hard stop-and-go cycles chew through components, whereas coasting down smoothly stretches both gas mileage and brake life.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: What safety and cost risks come from poor vehicle upkeep, and how do underinflated tires hurt efficiency?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Deferred maintenance raises operating costs and breakdown crash risk while soft tires drag down miles per gallon.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: What training costs can Wisconsin's Driver Education Grant Program cover for income-eligible teens?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Qualifying families can have state grant funds cover classroom lessons, in-car instruction, or the entire package.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: Do age or past medical conditions disqualify someone from registering as an organ and tissue donor?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Never rule yourself out ahead of time because people of every age and medical background can register.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: Once you turn eighteen, can relatives override your organ donor registration, and why still talk with family?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Your adult donor registration is legally final against anyone's objection, yet sharing your wishes spares family surprise.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: Even though an eighteen-year-old's donor choice cannot be overturned by relatives, what step does the handbook still urge?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Letting loved ones know ahead of time honors your unchangeable adult decision without confusion during an emergency.
